items.text: The Finance Minister of Tamil Nadu, Dr. N. Marie Wilson, presented the Budget for the financial year 2026-27 on August 5, 2026. Budget Highlights The Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of Tamil Nadu for 2026-27 (at current prices) is projected to be Rs 40,67,312 crore, amounting to a growth of 14% over 2025-26. Expenditure (excluding debt repayment) in 2026-27 is estimated to be Rs 4,72,585 crore, an increase of 9% over the revised estimate of 2025-26. In addition, debt of Rs 51,971 crore will be repaid by the state. Receipts (excluding borrowings) for 2026-27 are estimated to be Rs 3,50,766 crore, an increase of 13% over the revised estimate for 2025-26. Revenue deficit in 2026-27 is estimated to be 1.4% of GSDP (Rs 55,775 crore), lower than a revenue deficit of 1.9% of GSDP (Rs 69,219 crore) in 2025-26 as per revised estimates. Fiscal deficit for 2026-27 is targeted at 3% of GSDP (Rs 1,21,819 crore). In 2025-26, as per the revised estimates, fiscal deficit is expected to be 3.5% of GSDP, higher than budgeted (2.9% of GSDP). Policy Highlights Gold schemes: Eligible women will be given an eight-gram gold coin and a silk saree as a wedding gift under Annan’s Seer Scheme. The scheme has been allocated Rs 812 crore.

items.text: Policy Highlights Gold schemes: Eligible women will be given an eight-gram gold coin and a silk saree as a wedding gift under Annan’s Seer Scheme. The scheme has been allocated Rs 812 crore. Further, under Thaaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam, a gold ring of one gram will be given to newborns delivered in government hospitals. The scheme has been allocated Rs 560 crore. Midday scheme: The Chief Minister’s breakfast scheme has been expanded to cover students from classes six to eight in government and government-aided schools. The outlay for the scheme is Rs 710 crore. Education: A scheme will be implemented for modernising government schools, with an estimated outlay of Rs 300 crore for 2026-27. Further, under the Vetri Laptop Scheme, college students will be provided with laptops. It has been allocated Rs 2,000 crore. Agriculture: Five goats or sheep will be provided for free to widows, deserted women, transgender persons, and persons with disabilities in rural areas. Rs 110 crore has been allocated to the scheme. AI development: The AI Industry Development Program will be implemented to curate specialised curriculum for higher education. It aims to skill five lakh youth by 2031. Further, an AI and innovation city ‘Arivagam’ will be developed to provide a collaborative and innovative ecosystem for AI companies and research institutions. Tamil Nadu’s Economy GSDP: In 2025-26, Tamil Nadu’s GSDP (at constant prices) is estimated to grow by 11% over the previous year. In comparison, India’s GDP is estimated to grow by 8% in 2025-26. Receipts in 2026-27 Tax Revenue Mobilisation The state’s own tax-to-GSDP ratio has ranged around 5.8-6.5% of GSDP since 2017-18. This ratio indicates a state’s ability to generate taxes from economic activities. As per a study commissioned by the 16 th Finance Commission, factors for stagnant revenue level include adjustment to new system of GST and closure of 1,500 liquor shops. In July 2026, the state government set up a Committee (Chair: Dr Montek Singh Ahluwalia) to recommend measures for revenue augmentation. Sources: Tamil Nadu State Government Finances, submitted by Madras School of Economics to the 16 th FC; Report of the 16 th FC, 2026; PRS. Total revenue receipts for 2026-27 are estimated to be Rs 3,50,027 crore, an increase of 13% over the revised estimate for 2025-26. Of this, Rs 2,54,575 crore (73%) will be raised through own resources , and Rs 95,452 crore (27%) will come from the centre. Resources from the centre will be in the form of share in central taxes (18% of revenue receipts) and grants (9% of revenue receipts). items.text: PRS. Revenue deficit : It is the difference of revenue expenditure and revenue receipts. A revenue deficit implies that the government needs to borrow to finance those expenses which do not increase its assets or reduces its liabilities. The budget estimates a revenue deficit of Rs 55,775 crore (1.4% of GSDP) in 2026-27. Fiscal deficit : It is the excess of total expenditure over total receipts. This gap is filled by borrowings by the government and leads to an increase in total liabilities. In 2026-27, the fiscal deficit is estimated to be 3% of GSDP. The 16 th Finance Commission has recommended the fiscal deficit target for states to be 3% of GSDP for the 2026-31 period. 50-year interest free loans for capital expenditure given by the central government will be excluded to arrive at the borrowing ceiling. In 2026-27, central capex loan is estimated to be 0.1% of GSDP (Rs 4,000 crore). As per the revised estimates, in 2025-26, the fiscal deficit of the state is expected to be 3.5% of GSDP, higher than the budget estimate (2.9% of GSDP). In 2025-26, central capex loan is estimated to be 0.2% of GSDP (Rs 7,000 crore) as per revised estimates. Outstanding liabilities : Outstanding liabilities are the accumulation of total borrowings at the end of a financial year. Annexure 2: Recommendations of the 16 th Finance Commission for 2026-31 The Report of the 16 th Finance Commission (Chair: Dr. Arvind Panagariya) was tabled in Parliament on February 1, 2026. The recommendations will apply for the five-year period between 2026-27 and 2030-31. The 16 th Commission (FC) has recommended the share of states in the divisible pool of central taxes at 41%. Divisible pool is arrived at after excluding cost of collection and cesses and surcharges from the gross tax revenue collected by the central government. The share remains unchanged from the 15 th FC award period (2021-26). The 16 th FC has proposed revised criteria to determine the share of individual states. Based on the recommendations of the 16 th FC, Tamil Nadu will have a 4.10% share in the divisible pool of central taxes during the 2026-31 period, a marginal increase compared to the 15 th FC period (4.08%). The 16 th FC has recommended grants worth Rs 9.47 lakh crore over the five-year period. These comprise grants for:

items.text: The 16 th FC has recommended grants worth Rs 9.47 lakh crore over the five-year period. These comprise grants for: (i) urban and rural local bodies, and (ii) disaster management. The 16 th FC has discontinued the following grants recommended by the 15 th FC: (i) revenue deficit grants, (ii) sector-specific grants, and (iii) state-specific grants. Grants recommended for Tamil Nadu over the 2026-31 period include: (i) Rs 25,069 crore for urban local bodies, (ii) Rs 16,930 crore for rural local bodies, and (iii) Rs 8,486 crore as disaster management grants. items.text: 2 2 The Department provides its services with transparency and delivers direct public services through the use of cutting edge technology, automation and digitalization. Committed to providing legal security and permanence to property transactions, the Department has undergone transformative reforms to align with the evolving needs of citizens and technological progress. In this pursuit, the Department is steadfastly pursuing the implementation of STAR 3.O, a comprehensive upgrade of STAR 2.O. Through STAR 3.O, the Department's operations have been enhanced to provide citizens with facilities such as Anywhere Registration, Paperless Registration and Presenceless Registration, enabling them to complete registration services from any location without having to visit a Sub-Registrar Office. This initiative has been designed to save the public's time and provide 3 them the confidence that their property transaction registration details are maintained securely and reliably. Furthermore, by utilizing Block Chain Technology, the system ensures that data is stored based on authenticated date and time of records, thereby enhancing the credibility and integrity of document registration. This technology also helps expedite the registration process and reduces the possibility of fraudulent practices. To further enhance service delivery and citizen engagement, there is a proposal to establish a unified call centre and unified service centre, within the Registration Department, ensuring a seamless e-service framework. The Department has also leveraged social media platforms to create public awareness regarding various initiatives, services and digital advancements, fostering greater transparency and accessibility. 3 2 The Department provides its services with transparency and delivers direct public services through the use of cutting edge technology, automation and digitalization.

items.text: The Department has also leveraged social media platforms to create public awareness regarding various initiatives, services and digital advancements, fostering greater transparency and accessibility. 4 4 To fortify the integrity of property transactions, the Government have introduced real-time biometric authentication and whenever biometrics of both executant and claimant do not tally with Aadhaar database, consent based IRIS scan authentication is carried out. This multi-layered security measure acts as a robust fraud prevention mechanism, reinforcing public trust in the registration system. Additionally, the introduction of the Tatkal Scheme has expedited the registration process, ensuring swift service delivery for time-sensitive transactions. The Department has achieved a landmark milestone in digital governance by ensuring adoption of the complete digitization of land records, thereby prohibiting the registration of classified Government lands. This decisive step prevents unauthorized transactions, ensuring transparency and accountability in land dealings. 5 Another transformational initiative is the availability of online certified copies of documents dating back to 1865 which reduced the need for retrieval of physical document while significantly enhancing ease of validation thereby eliminating the need for public to visit the Sub-Registrar Office. Furthermore, the introduction of the e-stamping facility has enabled direct and secure Stamp Duty payments, thereby minimizing discrepancies and improving efficiency. Recognizing the critical role of capacity building and continuous learning, the Registration Training Institute, located in Triplicane, Chennai, serves as a premier hub for Training and Development. Through training programmes structured by the above Training Institute, officials are equipped with expertise in registration laws, digital governance and fraud prevention mechanisms.

Through these ground-breaking reforms, digital governance advancements and citizen-centric initiatives, the Registration Department of Tamil Nadu continues to redefine efficiency. By harmonizing technological innovations with Citizen Welfare, the Department sets new standards in governance, revenue generation and institutional integrity, cementing its pivotal role in Tamil Nadu’s administrative and economic framework. 2. History of the Registration Department The Registration Department of the Government of Tamil Nadu has been consistently serving the public since its establishment in 1864. The General Registrar Office and District Registrar Office of Madras were formally set up on 7 January 4, 1865 laying the foundation for a structured registration system in the State. It is truly remarkable that a Department, which started in 1865 with a modest revenue collection of just Rs.1,42,871/- in its first financial year (1865-1866), has grown into one of the Tamil Nadu’s leading revenue-generating bodies, generating an impressive Rs.25,546.13 crore in revenue for the financial year 2025-2026. This phenomenal growth highlights the Department’s essential role in the State’s economic structure, showcasing its efficiency, adaptability and steadfast dedication to public service. 3.

Acts administered absolutely by the Registration Department The following Acts are wholly administered by the Registration Department:- Sl. No. Act Functions 1. The Indian Registration Act, 1908 The Indian Registration Act, 1908 delineates the enactments relating to registration of documents. The Act elaborates about the documents which are compulsorily registered and optionally registered. Additionally, it confers the procedure to be followed during registration and the mandatory registers to be maintained and the registration table fee to be collected for different kinds of documents. 2. The Indian Stamp Act, 1899 The Indian Stamp Act, 1899 stipulates the rates of stamp duty and the procedures for the stamp duty collected for 9 9 the various types of documents and also prescribes the mechanism for collection of stamp duty. 3. Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act, 1975 and Rules. The Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act, 1975 enacts a procedure for the registration of societies and its functions started for various purposes like literary, scientific, educational, sports, etc. Besides, it set forth the forms to be filed periodically. 4. The Chit Funds Act, 1982 The Chit Funds Act, 1982 manages the Chit Fund Companies and its regulations. This Act bestows the procedure for registering the Chit Fund Companies, regulations of conduct of Chits and makes provisions for the Arbitration which redress the disputes between subscriber and the Chit Fund Companies. 10 10 3.2. items.text: Zonal Offices – Headed by Deputy Inspector General of Registration The State is divided into 11 zones, with each zone administered by a Deputy Inspector General of Registration. These officers oversee the work of District Registrars and Sub-Registrars within their zones. Their duties include monitoring revenue collection, conducting inquiries and carrying out surprise inspections of registration offices. They are also acting as the appellate authority for determining the value of the plots in the layout which are fixed by the District Registrars. 4.2.2. Zonal Assistant Inspector General of Registration There are four Zonal Assistant Inspectors General of Registration stationed in Chennai, Coimbatore, Tiruchirappalli and Madurai. The main responsibility of the Audit Wing is to scrutinize diligently all the documents registered in the Sub-Registrar Offices and to check the revenue losses or the procedural lapses. The Deputy Inspector General of Registration, Zonal Assistant Inspector General of Registration will supervise the work of their jurisdictional Audit District Registrars. If any loss of revenue is identified, statutory action initiated for recovery under sections 33(A) or 47(A)(3) of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 and Section 80(A) of the Registration Act, 1908. In addition, compliance is ensured by making relevant entries in the Encumbrance Certificate thereby restricting further registration until the deficit amount is fully recovered. 17 4.2.5 Sub-Registrar Offices – Headed by Sub-Registrar At present, there are 595 Sub-Registrar Offices operational under Registration Department. items.text: 5. Registration Training Institute The Registration Training Institute has been established at Chennai on 25.10.1996. items.text: Estimation of the Market Value Guidelines Stamp Duty and Registration Fee were collected earlier for the value mentioned in the document as there was no way to determine the value of the documentary assets submitted for registration. Due to this, the value of the documentary assets was understated. This resulted in the loss of revenue to the Government. To avoid this, the concept of Guideline Register was introduced in the year 1967. A new section called 47AA was introduced in the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 vide Tamil Nadu Amendment Act 13/2008. This paved the way for preparing "Market Value Guidelines" through legally formed committees. The Government notified Tamil Nadu Stamp (Constitution of Valuation Committee for Estimation, Publication and Revision of Market 27 Value Guidelines of Properties) Rules, 2010 on 01.06.2010. The rules specified the procedures to be followed regarding the preparation of market value guidelines and the details of the members in the District Level Valuation Sub-Committee. The Valuation Sub-Committee consists of: 1. District Collector – Chairman 2. District Revenue Officer 3. Deputy Inspector General of Registration 4. District Registrars of the Concerned Registration District 5. District Registrar of the Headquarters of the concerned Revenue District Secretary 6. Assistant Director of Town Panchayats 7. Assistant Director of Panchayats 8. Regional Director of Municipalities and 9. Representatives of Local Bodies. 27 26 7. The societies which are registered under Societies Registration Act are mandated to ensure at least one General Body Meeting conducted every year and audited accounts filed with the District Registrar every year. Delay in filing 38 38 of annual returns is condoned by the District Registrar for a period upto 10 years, by the Inspector General of Registration for a period upto 20 years and by the Government beyond the period of 20 years. items.text: Chits The Chit Funds Act, 1982 aims to regulate Chit Funds, an indigenous business in India to ensure transparent operations and protect the financial interests of participants. It is very helpful for the people’s savings, capital mobilization and industrial and entrepreneur growth. The Chit Business and activities of Chit Fund Companies are regulated and monitored under the Chit Funds Act, 1982 and the Tamil Nadu Chit Fund Rules, 1984. At the State Level, the Inspector General of Registration is the Registrar of Chits in Tamil Nadu. Additional Inspector General of Registration is designated as Additional Registrar of Chits. In respect of Chit activities, Deputy Inspectors General are designated as Joint Registrar of Chits, District Registrars are designated as Deputy Registrar of Chits and 44 44 Sub-Registrar (Chit and Society) are designated as Assistant Registrar of Chits. Registration of Marriages The marriages solemnized are being registered by this Department under The Special Marriage Act, 1954, The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and The Tamil Nadu Registration of Marriages Act, 2009. The Sub-Registrars act as Registrar of Marriages under the said Act and marriages solemnized in the State are to be registered compulsorily under the Tamil Nadu Registration of Marriages Act, 2009. The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 In India, marriages among Hindus are governed by the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Section 8 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, deals with the registration of Hindu marriages in the Hindu Marriage Register. 53 Suyamariyathai (Self-Respect) Marriages or Seerthirutha (Reformative) Marriages solemnized between two Hindus are registered under Section 7A of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 The Special Marriage Act, 1954 regulates and registers marriages solemnized in the country specifically those not conducted under personal religious laws. However, the Act does not mandate that individuals renounce their religion to register a marriage under its provisions. Under this Act, a Marriage Officer specifically a Sub-Registrar conducts and registers the special marriage. Under this Act, Marriage Registrars are empowered to solemnize marriages under Section 12 and to register any marriage that has already taken place under Section 15. 53 52 Act and Deputy General of Registration are appointed as Appellate Authorities.

The RERA Act, 2016 does not permit the execution of sale deed with respect to UDS land only. The commercial multi-storey apartments real estate projects are advertised and sold to the public by real estate companies based on the aggregate value that is the composite value (value of undivided land area plus value of building) on square feet only. However, before 01.12.2023 in respect of first sale of such projects, sale deed was registered only for the undivided share of land. A separate construction agreement document was registered in respect of the buildings. Due to this, the sale document of the apartment authenticating the conveyance of rate of the building from the promoters to the buyer is not available. In all the neighbouring 83 States, in respect of first sale of apartment / flats, only the sale document is registered in respect of undivided share of land area with building based on the composite value only. Therefore, in the interest of the public, the Government have issued an order to register the sale document in respect of first sale of flats / apartments in a real estate project, based on the composite value (i.e., the aggregate value of UDS of land and building) from 01.12.2023.

The Historical Journey of Taxation in Tamil Nadu The evolution of the taxation in Tamil Nadu originated with Madras General Sales Tax Act, 1939, that paves the first instance of a formal taxation system within the country. Commenced on October 1, 1939, the act demonstrated immediate fiscal viability, yielding a first-year revenue collection of Rs.439 lakh. This foundational legislation was subsequently superseded by the Tamil Nadu General Sales Tax Act, 1959 (effective April 1, 1959), and later modernized through the Tamil Nadu Value Added Tax Act, 2006, which came into force on January 1, 2007, to eliminate multi point taxation system.

items.text: This foundational legislation was subsequently superseded by the Tamil Nadu General Sales Tax Act, 1959 (effective April 1, 1959), and later modernized through the Tamil Nadu Value Added Tax Act, 2006, which came into force on January 1, 2007, to eliminate multi point taxation system. 2 2 The most significant taxation reform occurred with the enactment of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Act, 2017. Implemented nationwide on July 1, 2017, this legislation sought to mitigate the cascading effect of taxation by subsuming various Central and State indirect levies into a unified, singular tax regime. This taxation system has enabled a streamlined and integrated tax administration and designed to facilitate ease of commerce and fiscal efficiency. 2. Importance of the Commercial Taxes Department The Commercial Taxes Department functions as a primary architect of the State's fiscal stability, ensuring robust revenue mobilization through the effective administration of tax legislation. The revenue secured by the Department is indispensable, serving as a financial bedrock for the Government's extensive welfare portfolio and public development initiatives. Beyond its revenue functions, the Department is dedicated to institutionalizing a culture of statutory compliance by integrating 3 3 global best practices into its regulatory framework. By optimizing administrative workflows and enhancing the ease of doing business, the Department promotes a high- growth economic ecosystem designed to attract and sustain large-scale industrial and commercial investments. 3. Statutory Framework of the Department The Department is entrusted with the administration of the Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax (TNGST) Act, 2017, prioritizing the streamlined collection of revenue under this statutory framework.

items.text: 3. Statutory Framework of the Department The Department is entrusted with the administration of the Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax (TNGST) Act, 2017, prioritizing the streamlined collection of revenue under this statutory framework. Furthermore, the Department retains jurisdiction over tax collection under the Tamil Nadu Value Added Tax (TNVAT) Act, 2006 and the Central Sales Tax (CST) Act, 1956, with respect to the following six commodities mentioned in Entry 54 of the State List (List-II) of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India:- i. Petroleum Crude ii. High-Speed Diesel (HSD) 4 4 iii. Motor Spirit (Petrol) iv. Natural Gas v. Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) vi. Alcoholic Liquor for Human Consumption Effective November 1, 2024, the fiscal oversight of Extra Neutral Alcohol and rectified spirit intended for the manufacture of alcoholic liquor for human consumption has been transitioned. These items are now excluded from the Goods and Services Tax (GST) ambit and are governed under the Tamil Nadu Value Added Tax Act, 2006. Additionally, the Department continues to manage the residual tax administrative functions and settlement of proceedings related to following legacy Acts that remained in force until June 30, 2017:– 1. Tamil Nadu Betting Tax Act, 1935 2. Tamil Nadu Entertainments Tax Act, 1939 3. Central Sales Tax Act, 1956 4. Tamil Nadu General Sales Tax Act, 1959 5. Organizational Framework of the Department The Commercial Taxes Department is presided over by the Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, who serves as the Administrative Head. Headquartered in Chennai, the Department's operational structure is divided into four primary functional wings. i. The Office of the Commissioner of Commercial Taxes: It functions as central executive and policy- formulating body. ii. Territorial Divisions: It ensures localized tax administration and compliance. iii. Intelligence Divisions: It is responsible for enforcement, investigation and the prevention of tax evasion. iv. items.text: These divisions are further sub-divided into CT Districts/Zones and Assessment Circles. Joint Commissioners are responsible for the overall supervision of these units and exercising the role of statutory revision authority over the orders issued by proper officers.  Each Commercial Tax District / Zone is administered by a Deputy Commissioner and there are 55 CT Districts/Zones. The responsibilities of the Deputy Commissioner are systemic monitoring of Assessment Circles for improving collections, review of orders passed by proper officers and to file state appeals before the first Appellate Authority and the collection of arrears. 15 15  In the Commercial Taxes Department, there are 338 Assessment Circles. Out of this, 244 Circles are headed by Assistant Commissioner and 94 Circles are headed by State Tax Officer. The designated proper Officer/Assessing Officers are executing various statutory functions such as registration, monitoring of return compliance, processing of refunds, return scrutiny, assessment formulation, and the recovery of revenue arrears. 7.1.1 Large Taxpayers Unit  Jurisdiction: The Large Taxpayers Unit functions in Chennai to facilitate large taxpayers of the State. It is formed in 2010 and administers top 123 State allocated GST Tax Payers and 26 VAT Dealers.  Revenue Impact: The Large Tax Payers Unit is contributing 29% of the gross tax revenue under GST 16 16 and 99% of VAT Revenue collected by the Department.  Performance Metrics: The revenue collection performance of the LTU for the preceding two fiscal years is detailed below:– Note: 1. The Intelligence Divisions have Data Analytics Unit (DAU) and inspections groups. A centralized Intelligence Wing is also functioning under the control of Commissioner of Commercial Taxes at the headquarters. 7.2.1 Formation of Intelligence Wing The number of Intelligence Divisions had been increased from 9 to 15 across Tamil Nadu in the year 2023. Of these, six new Intelligence Divisions viz., Chengalpattu, Tiruppur, Hosur, Tiruvarur, Virudhunagar, and Cuddalore were formed by carving out from the Divisions of Chennai-II, Erode, Salem, Trichy and Tirunelveli 18 18 Divisions on 01.08.2023, as per G.O.(Ms)No.19 from the Commercial Taxes and Registration (A2) Department, dated 09.03.2023.

items.text: 7.2.2 Functions of Intelligence Wings Major functions of Intelligence Wing comprised conducting inspections of the place of business and check the movement of goods vehicles to verify whether they are in consonance with the provisions of the GST Act. 7.2.2.1 Roving Squad Activity Roving Squads are utilized for the purpose of monitoring the movement of goods in transit which contravenes the Act/Rules. The identified contravention of the Act and Rules during the vehicular check includes Non-generation of Tax Invoices, e-Invoices for the tax payers whose aggregate turnover exceeding Rs.5 crore in any of the previous years, e-way bills and delivery to the place of business not registered under the GST Act. They book offences and collect penalty from the 19 19 offenders. Wherever, major offences are noticed, goods detention orders are issued and on payment of penalty under Section 129, the detained vehicles are released. The details of performance of Roving Squads are given below:– 7.2.2.2 Inspection Inspection Teams are conducting Inspection at the place of business of the Tax Payers and unregistered place of business/ godown etc., wherever there were sufficient reasons to believe that there is tax evasion made by the assesses. Consequent to the inspection made, determination of tax evaded/short payment/erroneous refund/ 20 20 Incorrect availment of ITC, Utilisation of ITC by reasons of Fraud/Wilful Mis-statement/ Suppression of fact made by the Intelligence Wing itself and communicated to the Territorial Wing for collection of arrears through a separate dedicated wing created for this purpose.

items.text: The performances of Inspection Team during inspection and through adjudication orders are detailed below:- 21 21 7.2.2.3 Special Steps taken for Improving the Selection of Units and Quality of Inspections  In order to augment the Revenue collection through Inspections, 14 Risk parameters with weightage points have been identified for selection of units for conducting Inspection and instructions have been issued to prepare the investigation files based on the risk parameters and weightage points. Till December 2023, all the investigation files are sent by the Field Joint Commissioners for approval for taking up inspections of the place of business. Thereafter, the monetary limit has been relaxed and all the Intelligence Divisions are directed to send the investigation files for the approval by the Headquarters in cases involving Revenue effect of Rs.1 crore above, so as to focus more on bigger entities rather than smaller one with the sole aim to generate more Revenue. 22 22  In addition, TSP 2.0 Data base had been created to provide crucial data like Total Turnover, Taxable Turnover, Exempted, Nil, Non-GST, Zero Rated Turnover, Tax paid in Cash and ITC etc., for selection of cases fit for inspection, so as to realize the Revenue.  In addition to relying on the data available within the Department data base, Third party data collected from TANGEDCO, Greater Chennai Corporation, Geology and Mining Department, Banks, Ministry of Home Affairs, GOI, are analyzed and fit cases have been selected and sent to respective Intelligence Division for taking up Inspections and remaining cases sent to the Territorial Divisions for Return Scrutiny.

items.text: 7.3 Review, Appeal and Revision Wing 7.3.1 Appeal  The appeals filed against the assessment orders passed under Goods and 23 23 Services Tax Act, 2017 and the Pre-GST Acts are handled in this wing.  For the Appeals against the orders passed under the Pre-GST Acts, such as Central Sales Tax Act, 1956, Tamil Nadu General Sales Tax Act, 1959, Tamil Nadu Value Added Tax Act, 2006 and other Acts, the Joint Commissioner (Appeals) / Deputy Commissioners (Appeals), is/are the First Appellate Authority. The Tamil Nadu Sales Tax Appellate Tribunal (TNSTAT) is the Second Appellate Authority.  For the Appeals against the orders passed/ decisions taken under the TNGST Act, 2017, the Joint Commissioner (Appeals) / Deputy Commissioners (Appeals), is/are the First Appellate Authority. The Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT) is the Second Appellate Authority. There were seven First Appellate forums (6 Deputy Commissioners and 1 Joint Commissioner) for GST Appeals. There were Nine First Appellate forums 24 24 (8 Deputy Commissioners and 1 Joint Commissioner) for Pre-GST Appeals.

items.text: 7.3.2 First Appeals under Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017  The Deputy Commissioners (Appeals) are the First Appellate Authorities for the appeals filed by the Tax Payers and the Department against the orders passed/ decisions taken by the proper officers 25 25 upto the cadre of Assistant Commissioners, under the Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.  The Joint Commissioner (Appeals) is the First Appellate Authority for the appeals against the orders passed / decisions taken by the proper officers in the cadre of Deputy Commissioner in Large Tax Payers Unit, Chennai.  The Departmental Representatives in the cadre of Deputy Commissioner and Assistant Commissioner will defend the revenue before the Joint Commissioner (Appeals) and the Deputy Commissioners (Appeals) respectively.  The details of appeals filed before the First Appellate Authorities under Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, upto the year 2025-2026, are tabulated below:– 26 26 Appeals pending as on 01.04.2025 Appeals filed during 2025-2026 Total Appeals disposed during 2025-2026 Balance as on 31.03.2026 45,420 40,991 86,411 8,356 78,055 7.3.3 Second Appeals under Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 The Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT), is the Second Appellate Forum to hear the appeals filed by the Department and Tax Payers challenging the Appeal Orders of First Appellate Authorities passed under Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax/Central Goods and Services Tax/Integrated Goods and Services Tax Acts, 2017.

items.text: The Joint Commissioner (Appeals) is the First Appellate Authority for the orders passed by the Assessing Officers in 28 28 the cadre of Deputy Commissioner in the Large Tax Payers Unit, Chennai.  The Departmental Representatives in the cadre of Deputy Commissioner and Assistant Commissioner will defend the revenue before the Joint Commissioner (Appeals) and the Deputy Commissioner (Appeals) respectively.  The details of appeals filed before the first Appellate Authority under the Pre-GST Acts during the year 2025-26, are tabulated below:– 7.3.5 Second Appeals under Pre-GST Acts  The Tamil Nadu Sales Tax Appellate Tribunal is the Second Appellate Forum for hearing the appeals filed by the Dealers / Department, against the 29 29 orders passed by the First Appellate Authorities under Legacy Acts.  The Main Bench of the Tamil Nadu Sales Tax Appellate Tribunal is located at Chennai, with 3 Additional Benches located at Chennai, Madurai and Coimbatore.  In Main Bench, the State is represented by the Joint Commissioner as State Representative and in Additional Benches, the State is represented by Deputy Commissioners as Additional State Representatives.  The details of appeals disposed by Tamil Nadu Sales Tax Appellate Tribunal 30 30 during the year 2025-26, are tabulated below:– 7.3.6 Review and Revision 7.3.6.1 Review and Revision under Goods and Services Tax Act  The adjudication orders passed/ decisions taken under TNGST Act 2017, by the jurisdictional Proper Officer are reviewed by the Territorial Deputy Commissioners and Intelligence Deputy Commissioners.  During the review, if the legality or propriety of an order is not found to be satisfied, an appeal is filed by the concerned Deputy Commissioner before the First Appellate Authority within 6 months from the date of communication of the orders.

The orders passed by the First Appellate Authorities are reviewed by the Territorial Joint Commissioners for deciding on filing second appeals before the Tamil Nadu Sales Tax Appellate Tribunal. Audit Wing  The newly created Audit Wing is effectively functioning with effect from 05.07.2023 and looking after audit matters under Legacy Acts and under the Goods and Services Tax Act.  Now, nearly 60 GST Audit units are functioning under the control of Joint Commissioners (Territorial) and they are 36 36 duly being monitored by the Additional Commissioner (Audit). 7.5.1 The Accountant General’s Annual Audit Audit is an inherent part of any tax Administration. items.text: Annual audit in the assessment circles is a periodic exercise by the Accountant General under TNVAT, CST and GST Acts, in respect of assessments, collections and refunds made. Besides, performance audit, the Accountant General does thematic study on different activities of the department from time to time. Presently, Accountant General is undertaking audit in selected Circles based on tax collection data. Further, performance audit on Assessment, Levy and Collection of GST on Minerals is also being undertaken by Audit in selected cases. Important audit observations pointed out by the Accountant General are discussed in the joint meetings of the Departmental Audit Committee and rectified. Besides, suitable replies, wherever necessary 37 37 circular instructions are issued with reference to the Accountant General’s audit observations. The rectification of Accountant General audit paras are closely monitored in Statement of Fact (SoF), Draft Para (DP) and Comptroller and Audit General of India Report (CAG) stages which resulted in collection of Tax amount of Rs.155.40 crore. 7.6. items.text: 38 38 7.7. Tax Research Unit 7.7.1 Functions:  To enhance the functioning of the Tax Research Unit, a Data Analytics Unit was established as per G.O. (Ms) No.88, Commercial Taxes and Registration (B1) Department, dated 29.07.2024.  The Tax Research Unit is responsible for monitoring the settlement of IGST to the State. As part of this process, unclaimed input tax credit under IGST was identified and the taxpayers were prompted to reverse such credits. This initiative resulted in an additional revenue of Rs.4 ,723.58 crore to the State exchequer through IGST settlement during the period from April 2025 to March 2026.  In addition to its core functions, the Data Analytics Unit (DAU) collects and analyses third-party data. In this regard, the DAU obtained property tax payment data from the Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency 39 39 (TNeGA). Through analysis, properties owned by tax defaulters were identified and the details were shared with field-level officers to facilitate recovery. 7.7.2 UPI Data Analysis:  Data Analytics Unit obtained data from UPI aggregators such as PhonePe, RazorPay, Paytm, GooglePay and Freecharge for analysis. On verification of the data, it was found out that 37,485 unregistered or cancelled taxpayers had received receipts exceeding the threshold limit of Rs.20 lakh during the financial years 2023–24 and 2024-25.  Commencing from November 2024, those cases have been periodically referred to field formations for physical verification.

The Policy Wing assists in decision-making through active participation in the meetings of GST Council, Group of Ministers (GoM), GST Implementation Committee (GIC), Fitment Committee, Law Committee and Committee of Officers constituted by GST Council. The key operational responsibilities of the Policy Wing includes preparation of draft amendments to the TNGST Act, 2017 and TNGST Rules, 2017 as per the recommendations of the GST Council and 48 48 issue of pari-materia circulars and notifications under the statutory provisions.

items.text: The key operational responsibilities of the Policy Wing includes preparation of draft amendments to the TNGST Act, 2017 and TNGST Rules, 2017 as per the recommendations of the GST Council and 48 48 issue of pari-materia circulars and notifications under the statutory provisions. 7.9.1 Salient features of GST:  State and Central GST is levied on intra- State supply of goods and services.  Integrated GST is levied on the import and inter-State supply of goods and services.  Two rate tax structure with a standard rate of 18% and a merit rate of 5%  De-merit rate of 40% for specified goods and services  Special rates of 3% on gold, silver, platinum, pearls etc., and 0.25% on rough diamonds, precious stones, semi- precious stones etc.  In general, supply of services attracts GST at 18%.  A composition scheme of taxation is available for taxpayers with an annual aggregate turnover limit of up to Rs.1.5 crore in the preceding financial year, with tax rates of 1% and 5% depending on the nature of business. 49 49  Composition tax for service providers with an annual aggregate turnover of up to Rs.50 lakh in the preceding financial year, is at the rate of 6%. 7.9.2 Goods and Services Tax Council The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A of the Indian Constitution. The Constitution (101 st Amendment) Act, 2016 provided the legislative framework for the creation of the GST Council. The Centre and all States including Union Territories having legislature are members of the GST Council.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Commercial Taxes department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The Constitution (101 st Amendment) Act, 2016 provided the legislative framework for the creation of the GST Council. The Centre and all States including Union Territories having legislature are members of the GST Council. The GST Council meets periodically to deliberate and decide on various issues related to GST such as, threshold limit of turnover for registration, principles of levy, goods and services that may be subjected to or exempted from GST, principles that govern place of supply, GST rates, special rates for raising additional resources during natural calamity or disaster, special provisions for certain States etc. Till 2026, the GST Council has conducted 56 meetings. 50 50 7.9.3 GST Council Meeting During the year 2026, the 56 th meeting of GST Council was held at New Delhi on 03.09.2025.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Commercial Taxes department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Till 2026, the GST Council has conducted 56 meetings. 50 50 7.9.3 GST Council Meeting During the year 2026, the 56 th meeting of GST Council was held at New Delhi on 03.09.2025. The GST Council has recommended the following rate rationalization reforms:–  Removal of 12% GST rate slab.  Reduction of GST to 5% on several common man items such as hair oil, toilet soap bars, shampoos, toothbrushes, toothpaste, bicycles, tableware, kitchenware, other household articles, etc.  GST exemption on Ultra-High Temperature (UHT) milk, paneer and all Indian Breads.  GST exemption on 36 lifesaving drugs and medicines and reduction of GST to 5% on all other drugs and medicines.  Reduction of GST to 5% on almost all of the food items such as butter, ghee, namkeens, bhujia, sauces, pasta, noodles, chocolates, coffee, preserved meat, cornflakes etc.  Reduction of GST to 5% on agricultural goods such as tractors, agricultural, horticultural or forestry machinery etc.

items.text: 51 51  Reduction of GST to 5% on various instruments and apparatus used for medical, surgical, dental or veterinary usage or for physical or chemical analysis, medical equipment and supplies such as wadding, gauze, bandages, diagnostic kits and reagents, blood glucose monitoring system, etc.  Reduction of GST to 5% on renewable energy devices and parts for their manufacture.  Reduction of GST to 5% without Input Tax Credit, on ‘Hotel Accommodation’ services having value less than or equal to Rs.7,500/- per unit per day or equivalent.  Reduction of GST to 5% without Input Tax Credit, on beauty and physical well-being services used by common man including services of gyms, salons, yoga centres, etc.  Correction of inverted duty structure for the manmade Textile Sector by reducing GST rate on manmade fibre from 18% to 5% and manmade yarn from 12% to 5%.  Correction of inverted duty structure in Fertilizer Sector by reducing GST on 52 52 Sulphuric Acid, Nitric Acid and Ammonia from 18% to 5%.  Reduction of GST from 28% to 18% on air-conditioning machines, televisions, dishwashing machines, cement, motorcycles of engine capacity not exceeding 350cc, buses, trucks, ambulances, three-wheelers, etc.  GST exemption on all individual life insurance and health insurance along with reinsurances thereof.

items.text: 7.9.4 Implementation of recommendations of 56th meeting of GST Council  The changes in GST rates of all goods and services except certain tobacco products like cigarettes, pan masala, gutkha and chewing tobacco products were implemented with effect from 22.09.2025.  The Compensation Cess levied at varying rates on tobacco and tobacco products like cigarettes, pan masala, etc., has been abolished with effect from 01.02.2026 and replaced by a new taxation structure with a 53 53 higher 40% slab under GST with effect from 01.02.2026. 7.9.5 Group of Ministers constituted by GST Council: Group of Ministers (GoMs) are constituted by GST Council to examine complex tax issues, deliberate on rate rationalization and recommend reforms for specific sectors. Tamil Nadu is a Member of various GoMs mentioned below:– 7.9.5.1 Group of Ministers on GST System Reforms The Group of Ministers on GST System Reforms has been constituted based on the recommendations of the GST Council in its 45 th meeting held in September 2021. The GoM focuses on reviewing Information Technology tools and interface available with tax officers, identifying potential sources of evasion and suggesting changes in business processes and Information Technology systems to plug revenue leakages, using data analysis for revenue augmentation and identifying mechanisms for 54 54 better coordination between Central and State tax administrations. 7.9.5.2 Group of Ministers on Life and Health Insurance The Group of Ministers on Life and Health Insurance has been constituted based on the recommendations of the GST Council in its 54th meeting held in September 2024.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Commercial Taxes department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: 7.9.5.2 Group of Ministers on Life and Health Insurance The Group of Ministers on Life and Health Insurance has been constituted based on the recommendations of the GST Council in its 54th meeting held in September 2024. The GoM has been mandated to examine and review the present tax structure of GST on life and health insurance and suggest GST rates on health insurance, life insurance and re-insurances thereof. The final report of the GoM was presented in the 56 th meeting of the GST Council held on 03.09.2025. The GST Council recommended to exempt all individual life insurance and health insurance along with reinsurances thereof and implemented with effect from 22.09.2025. 55 55 7.9.5.3 Group of Ministers on restructuring Compensation Cess The Group of Ministers on restructuring Compensation Cess has been constituted, based on the recommendations of the GST Council in its 54 th meeting. The GoM has been set up to make taxation proposal to replace compensation cess after its abolition. The final report of the GoM was presented in the 56 th meeting of the GST Council held on 03.09.2025. The GST Council recommended to abolish the Compensation Cess on fulfilment of obligations under the Compensation Cess account. 7.9.5.4 Group of Ministers on Analysis of Revenue from GST The Group of Ministers on Analysis of Revenue from GST has been re-constituted, based on the recommendations of the GST Council in its 55 th meeting held in December 2024.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Commercial Taxes department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: 7.9.5.4 Group of Ministers on Analysis of Revenue from GST The Group of Ministers on Analysis of Revenue from GST has been re-constituted, based on the recommendations of the GST Council in its 55 th meeting held in December 2024. The main functions of the GoM include State-wise revenue trend analysis, analysis of impact of economic and other factors on GST revenue, anti-evasion and 56 56 compliance tools integration and suggest policy recommendations for revenue augmentation. 7.9.6 Committees and Group of Officers under GST Council Several key standing Committees of Officers and Group of Officers from nominated States and Central authorities are constituted by GST Council to deliberate on legal drafting, tax rates, administrative implementation, grievance resolution and specific issues. Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Tamil Nadu is a member of the following Committees and Group of Officers formed by the GST Council:– 7.9.6.1 Goods and Services Tax Implementation Committee (GIC) The Goods and Services Tax Implementation Committee (GIC) has been constituted, based on the decision taken by the GST Council in its 14 th meeting held in May 2017. The GIC takes decisions on issues of urgent and procedural nature that arise between GST Council Meetings and subsequently places the decisions before the next GST Council meeting for 57 57 information and for taking decision, where necessary. 7.9.6.2 Law Committee The Law Committee has been constituted, based on the decision of the GST Council in its 14 th meeting. The Committee is responsible for the issues pertaining to GST Act and Rules and proposes amendments to remove difficulties faced in interpretation of law and also proposes circulars to clarify legal matters.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Commercial Taxes department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The Committee is responsible for the issues pertaining to GST Act and Rules and proposes amendments to remove difficulties faced in interpretation of law and also proposes circulars to clarify legal matters. Tamil Nadu opted for inclusion in the Law Committee and accordingly, the Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Tamil Nadu has been included as a Member from 10.02.2025. A meeting of the Law Committee was held in Chennai on 13.10.2025. 7.9.6.3 Fitment Committee The Fitment Committee has been constituted, based on the decision of the GST Council in its 14 th meeting. The Committee deals with issues pertaining to GST rates, exemption and clarifications required to resolve issues pertaining to rates. 58 58 7.9.6.4 Committee of Officers on IGST Settlement Based on the recommendations of the GST Council in its 54 th meeting, the Committee of Officers on IGST Settlement has been constituted. The Committee has been mandated to examine the legislative provisions, Rules and the current process followed by GSTN, in order to arrive at a more accurate IGST Settlement to States and also the Information Technology issues of the GST Departments. 7.9.6.5 Group of Officers on Risk based Registration process Based on the recommendations of the GST Council in its 55 th meeting, the Group of Officers on Risk based registration process has been constituted. The Group of Officers has been set up to analyse the GST registration process to make it more streamlined for genuine taxpayers, recommend detailed guidelines/parameters for risk based registration process and examine the amendments required in the relevant GST Act and Rules.

items.text: The Group of Officers has been set up to analyse the GST registration process to make it more streamlined for genuine taxpayers, recommend detailed guidelines/parameters for risk based registration process and examine the amendments required in the relevant GST Act and Rules. 59 59 The recommendations of the Group of Officers have been discussed in the 56 th meeting of the GST Council. The GST Council recommended the introduction of an optional simplified GST Registration Scheme wherein registration shall be granted on an automated basis within three working days from the date of submission of application in case of small and low risk applicants, who do not wish to pass input tax credit beyond Rs.2.5 lakh per month. This new system is operationalized with effect from 01.11.2025, to benefit majority of new applicants applying for GST registration. 7.9.6.6 Group of Officers for Intermediary Services Based on the recommendations of the GST Council in its 55 th meeting, the Group of Officers for Intermediary Services has been constituted. The Group of Officers has been mandated to analyse the provisions of place of supply for Intermediary Services under clause (b) of sub-section (8) of Section 13 of the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and to 60 60 recommend any amendments or clarifications to the provisions. The recommendations of the Group of Officers have been discussed in the 56 th meeting of the GST Council.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Commercial Taxes department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The recommendations of the Group of Officers have been discussed in the 56 th meeting of the GST Council. The GST Council recommended that the clause (b) of sub-section (8) of section 13 of Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 will be omitted and the place of supply for ‘Intermediary Services’ will be determined as per the default provision under sub-section (2) of section 13 of the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, i.e. the location of the recipient of such services. 7.9.6.7 State Co-ordination Committee The State Co-ordination Committee of Tamil Nadu has been created based on the recommendations of the GST Council in its 50 th meeting held in July 2023 to create State level Committees for better co-ordination between GST authorities from the State and Central Tax Administrations. The Commissioner of Commercial Taxes and the Principal Chief Commissioner of GST, Tamil Nadu & Puducherry Zone are the Co-chairs of this Committee. 61 61 The Committee shall engage in data sharing on important cases of evasion/audit, knowledge sharing, referring any issue that requires a change in Acts / Rules / Notifications / Circulars / Instructions to the GST Council Secretariat and making collaborative efforts on the issues pertaining to taxpayer grievances. During the year 2025-26, the Committee has conducted 2 meetings on 06.05.2025 and 04.11.2025. 7.9.6.8 Grievance Redressal Committee The State level Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC) has been constituted based on the decision of the GST Council in its 38 th meeting held in December 2019.

items.text: 7.9.6.8 Grievance Redressal Committee The State level Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC) has been constituted based on the decision of the GST Council in its 38 th meeting held in December 2019. The Committee has been established to examine and resolve the grievances being faced by the taxpayers on GST related issues. It comprises Central and State Tax Officers, representatives of trade and industry and other GST stakeholders. The Commissioner of Commercial Taxes and the Principal Chief Commissioner of GST, Tamil Nadu & Puducherry Zone are the Co-chairs of this Committee. During the year 2025-26, the Committee has conducted 2 meetings on 06.05.2025 and 05.12.2025. 62 62 7.9.7 National Co-ordination Meeting The National Co-ordination Meeting serves as a platform to discuss various issues on greater co-ordination on GST administration and sharing of best practices by both Centre and States. The officers from Centre, States/Union Territories, GST Council Secretariat and GST Network participate in the meeting. During the 4 th National Co-ordination Meeting held on 10.11.2025, it was decided to constitute Working Groups of Officers to examine processes related to GST administration for recommending reforms, in order to enhance stability and predictability in the tax system. The Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Tamil Nadu has been included as a member in 2 Working Groups on GST Returns Processes and Co-working spaces. 63 63 7.10.

Authority for Advance Ruling and the Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling 7.10.1 Advance Ruling Authority (AAR)  Under the GST Act, any person registered or desirous of obtaining registration may seek advance ruling on classification of goods or services or both, applicability of notifications, determination of time and value of supply, admissibility of ITC and liability to pay tax.  The Authority for Advance Ruling, Tamil Nadu, comprises the Joint Commissioner of State Tax and the Additional Commissioner of Central Tax as its members.  The Authority has been duly constituted and is functioning at 2nd Floor, PAPJM Building, Greams Road, Chennai–600 006 and its e-mail id is jcadvrul.ctd@tn.gov.in.  The details of applications disposed by the Advance ruling authority (AAR) for the 64 64 period of 01.04.2025 to 31.03.2026 are provided below:- Year No. of Applications Disposed 2025-26 80 7.10.2 Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling, Tamil Nadu (AAAR)  If an applicant is aggrieved by the order of the Advance Ruling Authority, he/she may prefer an appeal within 30 days from the date of communication of the order, before the Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling (AAAR) Tamil Nadu.  The Commissioner of State Tax and the Principal Chief Commissioner of Central Tax, Tamil Nadu are members of the Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling.

Recognising the importance of this wing, a new post of Additional Commissioner (Systems) has been created in the Office of the Commissioner of Commercial Taxes in November 2023 and the Systems Wing functions under the Additional Commissioner (Systems) from 01.01.2024. This Wing provides various e-Governance facilities to Department officials and taxpayers / dealers. (1) e-Governance  Computerization was introduced in the Commercial Taxes Department for the first time in the year 1973, by utilising the services of the Government Data Centre at Guindy, Chennai.

items.text: This Wing provides various e-Governance facilities to Department officials and taxpayers / dealers. (1) e-Governance  Computerization was introduced in the Commercial Taxes Department for the first time in the year 1973, by utilising the services of the Government Data Centre at Guindy, Chennai. This involved mainly the processing of returns and preparation of database for assessment details in the State. 67 67  The Commercial Taxes Department administers all e-Governance facilities for both taxpayers as well as departmental users through its own Information Technology Wing.  Separate IT infrastructure is maintained by the Department for Goods and Services Tax Act and Tamil Nadu Value Added Tax Act. (2) GST Interface Commercial Taxes Department has adopted Model-2 system in which back-office applications are supported by GSTN. The GST back-office system comprises of various modules namely Adjudication, Assessment, Demand and Recovery, Appeal, Intelligence and Audit. Various Notices and Orders issued in back-office are communicated to taxpayers only through the Common Portal. (i) Common Portal under GST  A Common Portal 'www.gst.gov.in' has been developed by the Goods and Services Tax 68 68 Network (GSTN) to facilitate all taxpayer related business processes under GST.  Under GST Regime, GSTN provides taxpayer interface through GST common portal and all taxpayers are performing their statutory requirements like new registration, amendment, filing of returns, refund applications, etc., through this portal. Also the Common Portal is used to issue communications like notice, order etc., by the officials to taxpayers.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Commercial Taxes department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Also the Common Portal is used to issue communications like notice, order etc., by the officials to taxpayers. (ii) Taxpayers under GST  In Tamil Nadu, as on 31.03.2026, about 12,40,109 active taxpayers doing business are availing the e-services rendered through the Portal.  Out of the above, 7,25,570 taxpayers are under the administrative jurisdiction of State Authority and the remaining 5,14,539 taxpayers are under the administrative jurisdiction of Central Authority.  The taxpayers are filing their monthly/quarterly returns through GST 69 69 Portal and paying their tax liability. After availing their eligible input tax credit, taxpayers are paying their tax dues in cash under various tax heads namely CGST, SGST, IGST and Cess. (iii) UPI Payments In a significant step towards enhancing taxpayer convenience, the Government of Tamil Nadu has facilitated GST payments through UPI and debit/credit cards from 7 th November, 2024. This facility simplifies the tax payment process by offering seamless and secured digital transactions, reducing the dependency on traditional banking channels. (iv) Interaction with GSTN Regular interaction and coordination is maintained with GSTN for continuous improvement of GST Common Portal and Back Office Portal by reporting issues in the existing system and identifying the new requirements to facilitate efficient and user friendly functioning of 70 70 the GST process from Taxpayers as well as officials side.

items.text: (3) VAT Interface A new improved VAT Portal https://tnvat. tn.gov.in/ctdportal/ has been made go live with effect from 01.11.2024 for Non-GST goods to facilitate the Dealers for smooth process of return filing, payment and registration, amendments, applying for saleable forms for Non-GST goods. The Portal is interlinked with IFHRMS to facilitate tax payment by the taxpayers. As of now, under TNVAT Act, 4,154 tax payers are filing their monthly returns in VAT Portal and pay their tax liabilities. (4) Big Data Analytics Solution In order to open up avenues of additional revenue to the State, to analyse revenue leakage and improvise revenue growth, the Commercial Taxes Department has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Indian Institute of 71 71 Technology-Hyderabad, engaging it as Application Service Provider for providing Big Data Analytics Solution services for three years with effect from 07.12.2023. (i) Goods and Services Tax Research and Analysis Unit  Goods and Services Tax Research and Analysis Unit was formed on 24.07.2024 to implement the Project of Big Data Analytics and IT Support Systems in coordination with the Application Service Provider.  Accordingly, for Revenue Augmentation, Notices have been generated based on various input parameters provided by the Unit enabling effectiveness & uniformity in scrutiny of large number of taxpayers in a short span of time.  A revenue of Rs.6,219.98 crore has been realized during the period from 31.12.2023 to 31.03.2026, based on the scrutiny for the assessment years from 2018-19 to 2023-24.

items.text: 72 72 (ii) Total Solution Project 2.0  With the support of ELCOT and TNeGA, the upgraded version of the Project named as “Total Solution Project 2.0 (TSP 2.0)” has been launched with effect from 23.12.2023 for the continuance of total e-Governance solution.  Back-office Application of the Commercial Taxes Department has been migrated from Model-1 System to Model-2 System from 05.09.2022. Subsequent to this, various Management Information System (MIS) reports are being generated by IIT-Hyderabad and deployed in TSP 2.0, for monitoring the activities of Department officials. (5) Protecting the State revenue by acting on Bill traders (i) Biometric Authentication  The Tamil Nadu State Commercial Taxes Department has successfully established a total of 49 Biometric Verification 73 73 Centres across the state (out of which 8 are provided by CBIC), enhancing transparency and efficiency in the GST registration process.  These centres, operational from January 28, 2025, have been mapped to 18 Divisions and 338 Circle Offices on the GST Back Office Portal, ensuring seamless accessibility for taxpayers.  To enable efficient biometric authentication, 55 booths have been established within these centres, each equipped with computers, iris scanners and web cameras.  These centres play a pivotal role in verifying new GST registration applications where Aadhaar authentication has not been completed, by capturing photo and document verification and for selected categories of Aadhaar-authenticated applications, they conduct biometric verification and document verification process. 74 74 (ii) ARAN Application  In order to facilitate the process of Street Survey, ARAN application has been implemented.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Commercial Taxes department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: 74 74 (ii) ARAN Application  In order to facilitate the process of Street Survey, ARAN application has been implemented. The officials carrying out Street Survey are provided with application level support where the taxpayer details are made available.  This application helps to identify the availability of taxpayer at the registered place of business, identify any unregistered business or additional place of business, taxpayer mapped to wrong jurisdiction. This also helps to check the Bill Trading Activities among other things. (iii) Welcome Letter  The process of issuing Welcome Letters to the newly registered taxpayers has been implemented in Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department from 75 75 July 2024 and they have been dispatched to all newly registered Dealers who registered from April, 2024 onwards.  This initiative aims to extend a goodwill gesture to new taxpayers and curb the proliferation of bill traders at the outset by implementing a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for field formations.  The Territorial Joint Commissioners have been mandated to send a ‘Welcome Letter’ via Registered Post with Acknowledgement Due (RPAD) to all newly registered taxpayers.  As various forums emphasize the importance of eradicating non-existent taxpayers and bill traders, the Registered Post with Acknowledgement Due (RPAD) services are effective for verification at the initial stage.  Based on the returned letters, suspension or cancellation of the registration of bogus taxpayers is done with instruction of the Joint Commissioner. 76 76  Actions are also being taken on the cancelled tax payers to disallow the propagation of Input Tax Credit by blocking the ITC received by the beneficiaries of these taxpayers.

items.text: 76 76  Actions are also being taken on the cancelled tax payers to disallow the propagation of Input Tax Credit by blocking the ITC received by the beneficiaries of these taxpayers. (iv) Laptop for Officials With e-Office and work from anywhere environment in practice, 1,810 numbers of Laptops have been purchased and provided for the Officials from the cadre of Assistant Commissioner and above and Head of Offices in 2 Tier Circles during the year 2025-26. (v) 5G Smartphone and SIM for field survey In order to enable Territorial Officials in field survey to capture photo of place of Business with Geo location during field verification, 2 number of 5G enabled smartphones along with SIM cards have been provided to Deputy Commercial Tax Officers in each of the 338 assessment circles. 77 77 (vi) Digital Signature Certificates for Officials 3,500 numbers of Cryptographic Tokens (One Time) and Class-3 Digital Signature Certificates have been procured for Officials upto the rank of Deputy Commercial Tax Officers, so that orders and notices can be digitally signed and issued, ensuring authenticity and integrity. (6) Connectivity  The Department provides seamless network connectivity to all the field offices through TANFINET under the Total Solution Project 2.0, with an efficient network system.  In order to ensure uninterrupted connectivity across all the 138 locations, including data centres, a secondary network connectivity is also provided to all locations through BSNL.

items.text: (7) GST Prime  GST Prime (version 4) is an application software developed by National 78 78 Informatics Centre (NIC), to provide various MIS reports facilitating the tax administrators to analyse and monitor tax collection.  It also helps Intelligence officials to identify the defaulters and tax evaders. This system acts as an interface between GST Common Portal, e-way bill and tax administrators and provides actionable reports.  It also provides e-way bill analytics reports to enable the officials to monitor discrepancies reported by the taxpayers compared to their returns and identify suspicious activities of taxpayer. items.text: 8.2 State Level Taxpayers Advisory Committee  The State Level Taxpayers Advisory Committee has been constituted to redress the grievances of the taxpayers based on the representations and suggestions received from the Trade 83 83 Associations and Chambers of Commerce.  The Committee functions under the Chairmanship of the Commissioner of Commercial Taxes. 8.3 District Level Taxpayers Advisory Committee District Level Taxpayers Advisory Committees have been constituted with the District Collector as the Chairman for the purpose of redressing the grievances of taxpayers in their Districts. 8.4 Ease of Doing Business 8.4.1 Promotion of Ease of Doing Business The Commercial Taxes Department is committed to enhancing the ease of doing business by simplifying procedures, leveraging digital platforms and strengthening the taxpayer support systems. In this regard, the following initiatives have been undertaken:– 84 84 8.4.2 Key Initiatives  The core business processes such as Registration, Filing of Returns, Payment, and Refunds under GST have been fully digitalized and made accessible ‘online’, which reflects the current status of the Taxpayer details.  This enables easy handling of the Taxpayer issues related to Adjudication, Refund, Registration, Inspection, Audit, Appeal and Recovery of arrears. 8.4.2.1 Ease of Business Cell The ‘Ease of Business Cell’ is headed by a Joint Commissioner (ST) and functions under the control of the Additional Commissioner/ Director, CTSTI, Chennai.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Commercial Taxes department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: 8.4.2.1 Ease of Business Cell The ‘Ease of Business Cell’ is headed by a Joint Commissioner (ST) and functions under the control of the Additional Commissioner/ Director, CTSTI, Chennai. 8.4.2.2 Structure of Ease of Business Cell The Ease of Business Cell consists of the following three wings:– i) Grievance Redressal Wing ii) Quality Monitoring Wing iii) Social Media Wing 85 85 8.4.2.3 Functions of the Wings (i) Grievance Redressal Wing  The Grievance Redressal Wing plays a vital role in addressing the Taxpayer issues by handling queries and complaints through phone and email. Two mobile numbers and a landline number have been provided to the Grievance Redressal Wing to assist the taxpayers for clarifying queries, particularly those related to GST procedures and clarifications, enhancing accessibility and support.  During the year 2025-26, 3,306 queries have been successfully resolved, thereby significantly improving Taxpayer satisfaction and Departmental Responsiveness. (ii) Quality Monitoring Wing  The Quality Monitoring Wing ensures consistency and reliability in the orders passed by Proper Officers, 86 86 covering critical functions such as Registration, Refunds, Scrutiny, Audit, Inspection and Intelligence operations, with the objective of promoting uniformity and quality in tax administration.  As a special initiative, the process of Rectification of Adjudication orders have been closely monitored and through continuous follow-up, 15,279 Rectification Orders have been passed during the year 2025-26.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Commercial Taxes Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Commercial Taxes department]

items.text: (iii) Social Media Wing  The Social Media Wing facilitates effective communication with the stakeholders of the Departments by disseminating press releases and important updates through platforms like Facebook and X (Twitter), ensuring timely information flow and broader outreach.  Together, the above initiatives contribute to a more responsive and 87 87 Taxpayer-friendly administrative framework. 8.5 Outbound Call Centre  An outbound Call Centre is functioning in the Commercial Taxes Annexe Building at Greams Road, Chennai.  The Call Centre officials will call the defaulters and urge them to file returns and pay the tax dues in time.  The Call Centre officials are also monitoring the arrear payment defaulters. 9. New Initiatives and Achievements of the Department 9.1 Gross Revenue Collection The Commercial Taxes Department has collected a gross revenue of Rs.1,43,914.55 crore during the year 2025-2026, which is Rs.6,047.30 crore higher than the collection of Rs.1,37,867.25 crore in the previous year 88 88 2024-2025, registering a growth rate of 4.39 percent. 9.2 Re-organization of Department Appeal Forums There were seven First Appellate Forums (6 Deputy Commissioners and 1 Joint Commissioner) for GST Appeals. There were Nine First Appellate Forums (8 Deputy Commissioners and 1 Joint Commissioner) for Pre-GST Appeals. As per G.O. (Ms) No.155, Commercial Taxes and Registration (A1) Department, dated 05.11.2025, the First Appellate Forums in the Department were reorganized and 15 First Appellate Forums have been created from November 2025, i.e., one Joint Commissioner (Appeals) and 14 Deputy Commissioners (Appeals).

items.text: 9.3 Introduction of Residential Training i. In addition to the standard curriculum, the Commercial Taxes Staff Training Institute, Chennai, has prioritized several high-impact Residential and Specialized Training Programmes for the Year 89 89 2025-26 to enhance the Operational Efficiency of the Department. In this regard, the Government had allotted Rs.77,11,600/- and Rs.1,85,39,560/- under the Training Head of Account “2040-00-101-AC-37201”, for the implementation of the Residential Training Programmes. ii. In-Service Residential Training for promoted Deputy Commercial Taxes Officers, Induction Residential Training for Direct recruited Officials and Staffs i.e., Assistant Commissioners, Deputy State Tax Officers, Assistants, Junior Assistants, Typists and Steno-Typists have been conducted at various places in the year 2025-26. 10. Right to Information Act, 2005  The Commercial Taxes Department provides prompt information to all the petitions received from the general and mercantile public under the Right to Information Act, 2005.  During the year 2025, i.e., from 01.01.2025 to 31.12.2025, a total of 695 applications were received and replies have been furnished in all the petitions. 13. Its responsibilities extend beyond annual budget preparation to include resource mobilisation, expenditure control, debt management, employee compensation and pensions, financial devolution to local bodies, public-sector enterprise oversight, procurement, audit and relief administration. Through these functions, the Department seeks to maintain fiscal stability while ensuring that public resources are allocated efficiently towards welfare, infrastructure and developmental priorities of Tamil Nadu.

items.text: Mandate 44. The objective of audit is to provide policy makers with reliable and accurate information about the performance of Government Departments and Government Schemes. Audit insights can help them to allocate resources efficiently and effectively, improve public service delivery and maximize the value for public taxpayers. The mandate of the Director General of Audit is to ensure the Internal and Statutory audit functions of the Government Audit Departments are carried out effectively and for early identification of wrong doings and to initiate necessary corrective actions without delay and also, to enhance the capacity of the 52 55 Audit Departments and to infuse professionalism. Based on the mandate the DGA office is majorly divided into the followings functional wings. 1. Audit Quality 2. Audit Reforms 3. Performance Audit 4. Capacity Building and IT Key Reforms and Initiatives 45. As part of the endeavour to make the audit process more transparent and professional, several initiatives have been taken. Some of them are listed below: Comprehensive Audit Management System (CAMS): 46. Comprehensive Audit Management System (CAMS), a web-based platform aimed at the digitization and supervision of 56 all audit related task and procedures has been launched in all the Audit Departments. To enhance transparency and efficiency in the settlement of audit objections, the Audit Para Management System (APMS) module has been introduced within CAMS, facilitating a Faceless Settlement mechanism. Building upon these digital initiatives, necessary steps are being undertaken to introduce Faceless Audit in a phased manner across the Audit Departments. In order to ensure the effective implementation of CAMS and to promptly address queries from auditors and auditee institutions, a dedicated Help Desk has been established. Audit Reforms 47.

items.text: Audit Reforms 47. With a view to enhancing accountability and ensuring objective evaluation of scheme implementation, 54 57 Performance Audit has been introduced. Considering the need to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of public service delivery, Performance Audit is being accorded utmost importance. In order to ease the burden of audit compliance for smaller institutions, a checklist-based Template Audit has been introduced as part of CAMS across the Audit Departments. Further, delegations of Audit Teams have been deputed to other States to study and adopt the best practices being followed in those States. Audit Quality Management framework 48. The Tamil Nadu Infrastructure Development Board established under the Tamil Nadu Infrastructure Development Act, 2012 acts as the nodal agency for infrastructure development in the State. The Board primarily coordinates infrastructure development activities in the State and facilitates projects undertaken by Government institutions through the public sector mode as well as through Public- Private Partnerships (PPP) mode. Structure 113. The Chairperson of the Board is the Hon’ble Chief Minister (Ex-officio) and Vice Chairperson of the Board is the Hon’ble Minister for Finance (Ex-officio). Under the TNID Act, 2012, Tamil Nadu Infrastructure Development Fund (TNIDF) is set up for providing financial support to facilitate the design, development, functioning, administration, management of projects. Tamil Nadu Infrastructure Fund Management Corporation (TNIFMC) is an Asset Management Company established under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) Regulations, 2012. TNIFMC has been structured as a professionally managed, board-governed company aligned with the State’s Vision of strengthening Tamil Nadu’s leadership in business, industry, and commerce by attracting investments that drive sustainable economic growth and create employment opportunities. TNIFMC is owned 49% by the Tamil Nadu Infrastructure Development Board (TNIDB) and 51% by various financial institutions. The company currently manages three 136 thematic funds: the Tamil Nadu Shelter Fund (TNSF), the Tamil Nadu Emerging Sector Seed Fund (TNESSF), and the Tamil Nadu Green Climate Fund (TNGCF).
