items.text: FINANCE DEPARTMENT DEMAND No.50 Pension and Other Retirement Benefits POLICY NOTE 2026 - 2027 Dr. N. MARIE WILSON Minister for Finance, Planning and Development © Government of Tamil Nadu 2026 DEMAND No.50 PENSION AND OTHER RETIREMENT BENEFITS POLICY NOTE FOR 2026-2027 Tamil Nadu Government employees appointed under time scale of pay are covered by Defined Benefit Pension Scheme , Contributory Pension Scheme and Tamil Nadu Assured Pension Scheme . The employees appointed prior to 01-04-2003 are covered by Defined Benefit Pension Scheme, employees appointed from 01-04-2003 to 31-12-2025 are covered by Contributory Pension Scheme . The employees appointed with effect from 01-01-2026 are compulsorily covered by Tamil Nadu Assured Pension Scheme. TAMIL NADU ASSURED PENSION SCHEME (TAPS) Tamil Nadu Assured Pension Scheme (TAPS) is mandatory for all eligible Government servants who enter the Government service from 01-01-2026 and all eligible Government servants who were hitherto covered under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) and who were in service as on 01-01-2026. 2. The broad features of Tamil Nadu Assured Pension Scheme (TAPS) is as follows: (i) Assured monthly payout equal to 50% of the last drawn monthly pay. (ii) In case of death of the superannuated Government servant, monthly family payout to the eligible family members, equal to 60% of the monthly payout last 23 drawn by the superannuated Government servant. (iii) Entitlement of minimum payout for those coming under TAPS , as may be prescribed. (iv) Dearness Relief increases on par with serving Government servants. items.text: Speech of Dr. N. Marie Wilson, Minister for Finance, Planning and Development, Government of Tamil Nadu, presenting the Revised Budget Estimates for the year 2026 -27 to the Legislative Assembly on 5 th August 2026. Hon’ble Speaker, Paying my deep respect s to our ideological leaders — Thanthai Periyar, Perunthalaivar Kamarajar, Annal Ambedkar, Rani Velu Nachiyar and Makkal Sevagar Anjalai Ammal — I feel immense joy and pride in presenting the Revised Budget Estimates for the year 2026 -27 before this augu st Assembly, that holds the glorious legacy of being graced by great people cent ric leaders like Perunthalaivar Kamarajar, Perarignar Anna and Makkal Thilagam M.G.R. , who governed democratically with unwavering focus on public welfare and guide us through governance and administration even to this day. I also offer my heartfelt gratitude to our Hon'ble Chief Minister, the beloved leader of the people, who entered public life solely to pay back the debt of gratitude to the people who gave him everyt hing. He overcame numerous conspiracies to win a historic victory, for the sake of the people he loves as his own life and for the people who love him 2 as their own, and today he sits in this House as a true 'Jananayagan '. He constantly guide s us, offers counsel, and works tirelessly with the sole thought of delivering good governance to the people of Tamil Nadu. I express my heartfelt gratitude t o this leader cherished by the people .

items.text: He constantly guide s us, offers counsel, and works tirelessly with the sole thought of delivering good governance to the people of Tamil Nadu. I express my heartfelt gratitude t o this leader cherished by the people . I begin my address before this esteemed House with the timeless words of Thiruvalluvar , the supreme son , who gifted us the sacred Tamil scripture, Thirukkural: ”பிறப்ப ொக்கும் எல்லொ உயிர்க்கும் சிறப்ப ொவ்வொ பெய்ப ொழில் வவற்றுமை யொன் ” (குறள் – 972) “All are equal by birth; distinctions arise only from the deeds each performs ”. (Kural -972) 2. Guided by the noble principle that, 'All are equal by birth,' our Hon'ble Chief Minister, who has achieved numerous accomplishments within just three months of assuming office and has earned an enduring place in the hearts of the people , living in every household as a son, an elder brother, a younger brother, their very life, their kin and their every emotion . He is implementing many beneficial schemes for the people of Tamil Nadu who reside in his heart. 3 3. Our Hon'ble Chief Minister has brought about a massive people's revolution hitherto unseen in the political history of Tamil Nadu. This Government, founded on the great ideals of inclusive growth, social justice, equality, women's safety, eradication of poverty, a drug -free Tamil Nadu, and a corruption -free, h onest and transparent administration, has not only spoken of these ideals over the last three months, but has also demonstrated them through action. The people of Tamil Nadu have increasingly come to recognise that , this is a Government built on the enduri ng principles of genuine social justice and honest governance.

items.text: The people of Tamil Nadu have increasingly come to recognise that , this is a Government built on the enduri ng principles of genuine social justice and honest governance. 4. This Government, under the leadership of the Hon'ble Chief Minister, has recorded significant accomplishments across various sectors since assuming office: increasing the free electricity provi ded to consumers with bi -monthly consumption of up to 500 units, to 200 units and reducing their household expenses ; a loan waiver for farmers through co -operative societies; a special package for Kuruvai cultivation; the 'Singapenn Special Task Force' for women's safety; creation of Anti-Narcotics Task Force Units at the district level to root out the deep -seated drug culture in Tamil Nadu; closure of 717 liquor retail outlets 4 located near educational institutions, places of worship and bus stands that disrupted daily public life; and the 'Thaaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam' , to be implemented from 15th September, the birth anniversary of Perarignar Anna, for children born in G overnment Hospitals. The implementation of these schemes have reinforc ed the trust that people have placed in our Government. 5. The victory of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam is not merely the victory of a political party; it is the victory of the entire people of Tamil Nadu. Guided by this belief, and with the objective of implementing several welfare schemes for the benefit of the people, our Government, anchored in the core principles of Aram (Virtue), Porul (Prosperity) and Inbam (Well -being), has released the 'Vetri Tamizhagam – Vision Document' , comprising ten key focus areas.

items.text: Drawing on this document, the Government is identifying, formulating and operationalising programmes to be implemented over the next one, three and five years. This Government is co mmitted to making the necessary social, economic and human capital investments in Tamil Nadu — which has for many years been a leading State on several socio -economic indicators in India — into a poverty -free, prosperous State that offers equal 5 opportunity to all and upholds social justice, and to propel the State into a 1.5 Trillion dollar economy by the year 2036. 6. Taking this vision forward, the Government will implement the schemes listed in the Vetri Tamizhagam Vision Document, covering sectoral priorities which inter alia include empowering women, improving governance, providing housing for all, ensuring safe drinking water, generating sustainable livelihood opportunities, protecting social justice and promoti ng green cover. Th e first budget of this Government would lay the foundation for realising these visionary programmes . 7. Immediately upon assuming office, our Government released the 'White Paper on Financial Management' clearly indicating that Tamil Nadu's debt has doubled over the past five years, reaching about Rs.10 lakh crore. Further, Tamil Nadu has recorded fiscal indicators that trail behind other peer States, including State's Own Tax Revenue as a proportion of Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP), Re venue Deficit and Fiscal Deficit. Interest payments and committed liabilities as proportion of the State's Total Revenue Receipts, have been rising consistently, 6 leaving limited fiscal space for new schemes and programmes. 8.

items.text: Interest payments and committed liabilities as proportion of the State's Total Revenue Receipts, have been rising consistently, 6 leaving limited fiscal space for new schemes and programmes. 8. In these challenging circumstance s, this Government, having been elected by the people, is working on fulfilling its commitments to the public in a phased manner , while also taking various measures to recover the State from tight fiscal position. Firstly, the practice of requiring mandatory submission of unnecessary certificates by contractors in public tenders that had made tenders non -competitive; has now been abolished by this Government , thus bringing transparency to tendering process. Secondly , Government has discontinued the prevailing system of restricting tender eligibility to department's own registered contractors; and now, contractors registered with any Government department may bid for tenders issued by any other department, subject to the prescribed pre -qualification c riteria. Thirdly , to encourage young entrepreneurs and small businesses to bid for Government tenders for the first time, eligibility criteria for low -value procurements have been relaxed, giving new and emerging contractors easier access to Government ten ders. The resulting increase in competition is expected to bring greater efficiency to procurement and reduce fruitless expenditure. I am happy to inform this distinguished 7 House that these initiatives have already begun to yield positive results, deliveri ng significant cost savings for the State. 9. Before our Government had assumed office, a significant portion of tender ’s estimates were being cornered by few individuals and certain political parties. Our Hon'ble Chief Minister has achieved an unparalleled m ilestone by resolutely putting a complete end to this practice .

items.title: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister)

items.text: 9. Before our Government had assumed office, a significant portion of tender ’s estimates were being cornered by few individuals and certain political parties. Our Hon'ble Chief Minister has achieved an unparalleled m ilestone by resolutely putting a complete end to this practice . He has also changed the earlier procedure of approval at the Government ’s level for planning permission for multi -storied and high-rise apartment buildings. These approvals can now be obtained from Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority itself by delegation of powers, thereby eliminating the corruption that prevailed in the earlier process. Our Hon'ble Chief Minister remains steadfast in his resolve : "We will not touch a single paisa of the people's tax money. We will not allow anyone to touch it . If touched, we will not spare them . And we will not spare those who have touched it in the past ". He stands unshakeable in this resolve and seeing him and hearing his name , we witness corrupt individuals fleeing in fear every day. 8 10. While establishing transparency and integrity in tenders and project approvals, our Government is now also undertaking various measures for additional revenue mobilisation. As part of these efforts, Government has recently levied an additional privilege fee on liquor manufacturers. This is expected to mobilise an additional annual revenue of up to Rs.1,000 cro re to the exchequer. Government is also leveraging Information Technology through initiatives such as ' Faceless Assessment' under the Goods and Services Tax, ' Faceless Registration' in the Registration Department and end -to-end computerisation in monitori ng mining activities.

items.text: Government is also leveraging Information Technology through initiatives such as ' Faceless Assessment' under the Goods and Services Tax, ' Faceless Registration' in the Registration Department and end -to-end computerisation in monitori ng mining activities. These initiatives are together expected to generate additional revenue of approximately Rs.15,000 crore for the Government that will enable the implementation of many welfare schemes successfully . 11. To achieve growth in revenue receipts in tandem with economic growth , to expand revenue streams sustainably and to suggest measure s to increase the State's tax and non -tax revenue, the Government has recently constituted an expert committee on 'Revenue Augmentation' , headed by former Deputy Chairperson of Union Planning Commission, Thiru. Montek Singh Ahluwalia, along 9 with five other members. Through this Committee, Government aims to strengthen the State's fiscal autonomy and generate the financial resources necessary to fu lfil its socio -economic development commitments. items.text: The Government, under the leadership of our Hon'ble Chief Minister, administers Government schools in which more than 43 lakh students are enrolled. Ensuring a clean and safe learning environment in these schools is essential for quality education and the well -being of students. Currently, there is no integrated system in place to provide professional cleaning and security services in 10 Government schools. Taking this into consideration, the Government is set to implement the 'Super Clean Super Campus ' Scheme. Under this scheme, dail y cleaning activities, maintenance of drinking water facilities and toilets, and 24 -hour security for school campuses will be ensured, delivering Super Safety, Super Students and Super Campuses under our Super CM's governance. This scheme will be implemen ted in 10,000 schools in the first phase, with an allocation of Rs.139 crore in the Revised Budget Estimates for 2026 -27. 13. This is a Government led by our Hon'ble Chief Minister, the beloved Thaai Maaman of the children of Tamil Nadu. This Thaai Maaman and his Government recognise that quality educational institutions are just as essential as quality education itself for the children of Tamil Nadu. With the objective of modernising Government schools across Tamil Nadu and providing the necessary infras tructure facilities based on recommended norms, ‘Palli Niraivu Thittam ’ will be introduced. This scheme will cover a total of 3,734 schools, including 2,514 primary schools, 365 middle schools, and 855 high and higher secondary schools, at an estimated co st of Rs.2,132 crore. An amount 11 of Rs.300 crore is allocated for this scheme in the Revised Budget Estimates. 14.

items.text: An amount 11 of Rs.300 crore is allocated for this scheme in the Revised Budget Estimates. 14. With the objective of providing quality education to academically talented students from socio -economically disadvantaged backgrounds, the Gover nment will establish ' Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Schools of Excellence ' as modern residential institutions. These schools will cater to students from Classes IX to XII and will provide education, food, boarding, textbooks and uniforms free of cost. An amount of Rs.125 crore is allocated for the infrastructure development of these schools in the Revised Budget Estimates. 15. In a rapidly changing, globalised technological era, it is imperative that the school education curriculum be reimagined as experiential, inquiry-based, holistic, futuristic and competency - driven. A dynamic and progressive curriculum that focuses on critical thinking, creativity, financial literacy, gender equality, environmental awareness, digital competence, preparedness for competitive exami nations and global citizenship is necessary to prepare future -ready children. To make Tamil Nadu a leader in learning outcomes, an amount of 12 Rs.25 crore is being allocated towards revision of the School Education Curriculum . 16. "Say No to Drugs " has been the unwavering message of our Hon'ble Chief Minister, who has consistently urged the youth to "Choose Sports over Drugs ," recognising that the vision of a drug -free Tamil Nadu must begin in our schools. In keeping with the timeless wisdom of Avvaiyar's Aathichudi, " Ilamaiyil Kal ," children must be made aware from an early age of the dangers of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, alongside preventive education against substance abuse.

items.text: In keeping with the timeless wisdom of Avvaiyar's Aathichudi, " Ilamaiyil Kal ," children must be made aware from an early age of the dangers of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, alongside preventive education against substance abuse. Accordingly, Anti -Drug Clubs and student volunteer groups will be established in schools as part of this initiative. To strengthen awareness and facilitate timely reporting, the 10581 helpline number will be prominently displayed on all school campuses. Further, the Government has developed the ' Drug -Free Tamil Nadu ' mobile application, enabling students and teachers to confidentially and securely report information relating to drug trafficking and substance abuse. An amount of Rs.7 crore has been allocated for the implementation of this initiative. 13 17. With the aim of transforming Tamil Nadu's Public Libraries into state -wide digital libraries that function as learning and innovation hubs — featuring digital knowledge, universal membership, 24x7 internet and mobile access, digital content, free Wi-Fi, and co-working spaces at the 38 district central libraries — this Government allocates Rs.10 crore towards the redesign of Public Libraries. 18. Modern, branded bicycles equipped with helmets and water bottles will be provided to approximately 5.32 lakh Gen -Z stud ents studying in Class XI across Government and Government -aided schools in the current academic year. An estimated amount of Rs.277 crore is allocated towards this scheme. Our Hon'ble Chief Minister, deeply loved by Gen-Z, is firmly committed to nurturing them into a finest generation. This scheme reflects his vision and commitment. 19.

This scheme reflects his vision and commitment. 19. In the Revised Budget Estimates, Rs.44,527 crore has been allocated to the School Education Department. Higher Education 20. Tamil Nadu strongly opposes the NEET examination. Various irregularities and question paper 14 leaks in the NEET examination at the national level have severely affected the higher education prospects of the next generation . The Government of Tamil Nadu therefore urges the Union Government to immediately cancel the NEET examination system and revert to medical education admissions based on the earlier system of Class XII public examination marks. 21. A laptop has become an indispensable informat ion technology device for students pursuing higher education. In today's rapidly advancing digital era, laptops are invaluable assets for students to sharpen their technical expertise, undergo skill development training, and make effective use of their time. Recognising this, our Government will implement the ' Vetri Laptop Scheme ' for college students. With an allocation of Rs.2,000 crore, this initiative aims to equip students with laptops as an essential learning resource . 22. Guided by the timeless wisdom of Naaladiyar, " Knowledge is boundless, learning time is short ," it is our solemn duty to ensure that no student's learning is constrained by the unaffordability of decent accommodation.

items.text: 22. Guided by the timeless wisdom of Naaladiyar, " Knowledge is boundless, learning time is short ," it is our solemn duty to ensure that no student's learning is constrained by the unaffordability of decent accommodation. To transform student accommodation across the State, our Government will establish the ‘Tamil Nadu 15 Student Housing & Infrastructure Corporation ’ (TNSHIC) as a dedicated Special Purpose Vehicle, with an initial equity infusion of Rs.10 crore. Under the flagship ' TN-SUDAR ' (State Upgradation, Development and Advancement of student Residences) initiative, we will construct 200 Integrated Student Hostels delivering 1 lakh modern beds across major educational hubs. This project will be executed through a de -risked Public -Private Partnership (DBFOT) model, with an estimated ca pital outlay of Rs.3,200 crore, supported by a 20 per cent State Capital Construction Grant of Rs.640 crore, phased over the next two fiscal years. It will replace segregated housing with integrated, high-amenity campuses featuring fully air-conditi oned study hubs, 24x7 security, hygienic kitchens and an automated allocation framework designed to ensure diversity and social parity. In the years to come, TN -SUDAR will help integrate youth across diverse communities and faiths. 23. A specialised Government Law College, offering advanced legal education on par with a School of Excellence in Law, will be established in the academic year 2027 -28 at Madurai, with an intake of 300 students. To reduce the demand on petroleum based products and to help reduce environmental pollution, mechanics who currently service fossil -fuel-based vehicles, will be trained in the maintenance of electric vehicles and batteries, enabling them to service it well. Over the period of next five years, 2 2,500 persons, including 12,500 mechanics currently servicing fossil -fuel-based vehicles, will benefit under this scheme. An amount of Rs.3 crore has been allocated for this scheme in the current financial year. 25. With the aim of enabling Tamil Nadu youth to secure emerging global job opportunities, a new trade in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning will be introduced in Government Industrial Training Institutes at an estimated cost of Rs.10 crore. This trade will be introduced in 50 Industria l Training Institutes over a period of five years, at the rate of 10 institutes per year. Through this initiative, 24,000 students will receive training and employment opportunities in Artificial Intelligence technology over five years. Further, five new Industrial Training Institutes will be established in Tamil Nadu at a total 17 estimated cost of Rs.90 crore, for which an amount of Rs.7.5 crore has been allocated in the Revised Budget Estimates. 26. To ensure that the youth of Tamil Nadu are equipped with cutting -edge skills that make them employable and develop entrepreneurial interest, this Government will introduce the 'Vetri Skill Training Scheme '. Under this scheme, the Government will provide industry -aligned skilling to 12 lakh college students and 1 lakh unemployed youth in this year . In addition, internship training programmes will be provided in collaboration with Government and private industries to 20,000 youth in the first phase. During the internship tr aining period, 18 graduates and those with vocational education qualifications will receive a monthly stipend. Priority under this scheme will be given to youth from families without permanent employment. A sum of Rs.150 crore is being allocated towards the implementation of this scheme. 28. Recognising Artificial Intelligence as a pivotal driver of future economic growth and technological innovation, our Government is determined to position Tamil Nadu at the forefront of this digital transformation. To ensure ou r youth become the primary beneficiaries of this technology -driven revolution, I am pleased to announce the launch of the AI Industry Development Program . Under this programme, an expert committee of academic and industry leaders will curate specialised AI curricula tailored to higher education tiers.

items.text: To ensure ou r youth become the primary beneficiaries of this technology -driven revolution, I am pleased to announce the launch of the AI Industry Development Program . Under this programme, an expert committee of academic and industry leaders will curate specialised AI curricula tailored to higher education tiers. By leveraging state -of-the-art training infrastructure and strategic partnerships with premier institutions such as IIT Madras, we aim to skill and empower 5 lakh youth across engineering colleges, polytechn ics and ITIs by 2031, building a world -class, future -ready workforce. 29. In an era where Artificial Intelligence, Robotics and other emerging technologies are 19 transforming the world, the Tamil Nadu School Programme for Artificial Intelligence, Robotics and Kn owledge of online tools (TN SPARK) will be expanded to advance this vision. The programme will be extended during 2026 -27 from the existing 5,000 Government schools to additional 2,600 schools. Under the newly restructured three -tier framework, studen ts of Classes 6 to 8 will be introduced to the fundamentals of these emerging technologies; students of Classes 9 and 10 will receive intermediate -level training; and students of Classes 11 and 12 will be offered specialised elective courses. This initiat ive will directly enable students to innovate, develop leadership capabilities and strengthen Tamil Nadu's position in the global knowledge -driven economy. 30. items.text: 30. In the Revised Budget Estimates, Rs.2,022 crore is being allocated for the Labour Welfare and Skill Development Department. A vibrant sports culture serves as a powerful shield against social evils. To promote physical fitness, our Hon'ble Chief Minister himself ran 20 3 kilometre in the " Start Run, Stop Drugs " anti -drug run held at Marina Beach in Chennai, running shoulder to shoulder with thousands of youth to powerf ully convey this message. 32. With the message " Take Up Sports, Give Up Drugs ", this Government will launch an Integrated Youth Development Programme that will instil sporting discipline and civic responsibility among the younger generation instead of drug abuse . By integrating major youth organisations such as the National Cadet Corps (NCC) and the National Service Scheme (NSS) with the Health, Police and Social Welfare Departments, our Government will channel ize the energy of the younger generation towards sports, community service and well -being. Through the vision of " Sports for All, Sports Everywhere ," the campuses of our educational institutions will become safe and completely drug -free havens. 33. With the objective of winning gold medals at the Olympic Ga mes, our Government is firmly committed to elevating Tamil Nadu to the pinnacle of the global sports arena. To nurture elite sporting talent, 10 Olympic Centres of Excellence will be established across the State, with an allocation of Rs.50 crore.

items.text: To nurture elite sporting talent, 10 Olympic Centres of Excellence will be established across the State, with an allocation of Rs.50 crore. An alloc ation of Rs.5 crore is being made 21 to provide world -class training to select school students aged 8 to 18 who possess a passion and aptitude for sports . A further allocation of Rs.22 crore will provide financial assistance to 500 athletes excelling in natio nal and international sporting events. To take traditional Tamil sports to the global stage, an allocation of Rs.42 crore is made to conduct the Tamil Nadu Rural Sports Competition , alongside an allocation of Rs.2 crore to upgrade the infrastructure of the Tamil Nadu Physical Education and Sports University. 34. True sports development rests on twin pillars: creating world -class champions, and fostering a culture of everyday health and fitness among our youth. Sports must begin right from our schools. Curren tly, Government and Government -aided schools allocate only two sports periods per week for each class. To change this, structured sports and physical exercise activities of one hour per day will be introduced after school hours, with the required sports equipment and facilities provided to all Government and Government -aided schools. This will strengthen students' physical fitness, cognitive development, teamwork and discipline, while also helping identify talent capable of achieving success at the state, national and international levels. Further, to bring 22 sports to the common people, Neighbourhood Sports Facilities, small gymnasiums and sports complexes will be created in all blocks and urban local bodies. By building decentralised sporting infrastructure within walking distance of every young citizen's home, we will build a healthy, active and disciplined generation. 35.

items.text: In the Revised Budget Estimates, Rs.3,937 crore has been allocated to the Social Justice Department. 25 Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes, and De-notified Communities Welfare 43. Our Hon'ble Chief Minister is someone who has adopted Thanthai Periyar as his ideological leader . Our leader is not someone who deceives people in the name of social justice ; rather he is someone who has embraced it from the bottom of his heart . That is why our Government, under his leadership, remains firmly committed to upholding social justice in Tamil Nadu, and is undertaking every possible effort to safeguard Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent reservation. items.text: 55. In the Revised Budget Estimates, Rs.9,818 crore is being allocated for the Social Welfare and Women's Empowerment Department. 31 Health and Family Welfare 56. Maternal and child healthcare is a core pillar of Tamil Nadu's public health system. As per the recent National Sample Registration System survey, Tamil Nadu's Infant Mortality Rate stands at 11 per 1,000 live births, among st the lowest in the country, which has been made possible through the sustained implementation of public health schemes by the Government. As evidence of this, 99.9 per cent of deliveries in the State take place in hospitals, with over 53 per cent occurring in Government hospitals. To further increase deliveries in Government hospitals and thereby reduce the public's out-of-pocket healthcare expenditure, this Government will implement the ' Thai Maaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam' . Under this scheme, every newborn delivered in a Government hospital will receive a 1 -gram gold ring as a gift from the ir beloved Thai Mam man, the Hon'ble Chief Minister, commemorating the birth of the child and celebrating the joy and significance of motherhood. items.text: An amount of Rs.33 crore has been allocated for this scheme. 58. Maternity care and support centres under the na me 'Thai Care ' will be established across the State for pregnant women, who can stay at these centres to receive care as their delivery date approaches and benefit from the facilities . Free meals, medical support and continuous health monitoring will be offered at these centres, with an allocation of Rs.23 crore. 59. To ensure access to specialised medical care for people in remote and rural areas, the Government will establish a Telemedicine System based on a 'Hub -and-Spoke' hospital model. Five hubs staffed by specialist doctors will be linked to 200 spokes at Primary Health Centres and Government hospitals through an online network. The Government will also establish a 'Hub-and-Spoke' medical system for cancer care, transforming the ca ncer care hospital into an institution of State importance and an advanced treatment centre. A sum of Rs.10 crore is allocated in the Revised Budget Estimates for the preparation of a Detailed Project Report for this initiative. 61. The Hon'ble Chief Minister has ordered the waiver of agricultural loans amounting to Rs.5,932 crore, benefiting 14.43 lakh farmers, with this crop loan waiver being credited to the accounts of all eligible farmers. items.text: Beyond these measures, this Government, under the leadership of our Hon'ble Chief Minister, will remain steadfast in its commitment to the welfare of the farmers. 64. The Southwest Monsoon did not bring normal rainfall this year due to weather 35 phenomenon , resulting in insufficient water storage at the Mettur Dam. As a result, the dam could not be opened for irrigation on the scheduled date of 12 th June. Taking cognisance of this, our Hon'ble Chief Minister sanctioned the 'Kuruvai Package Scheme' at a total outlay of Rs.134 crore , to encourage paddy cultivation in both delta and non -delta districts and ensure no reduction in paddy production during the Kar, Kuruvai and Sornavari seasons. This scheme includes components such as mechanical paddy transplantation, direct seeding of paddy, seed production incentives, and the distribution of paddy seeds, liquid bio -fertilisers and micronutrient mixtures. 66. In the current financial year, 36 under the 'Vetri Magalir Goat Rearing Scheme' , five goats or sheep will be provided with a 100 per cent subsidy to destitute widows, deserted women, transgender persons and persons with disabilities living in rural areas, benefiting about 30,000 eligible persons. An amount of Rs.110 crore is allocated for this in the Revised Budget Estimates. 68. items.text: The Government aims to drive Tamil Nadu's Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) to a 1.5 Trillion US dollar economy by 2036, and is committed to building a friendly ecosystem that promotes industrial growth, attracts investment, and generates significant employment opportunities for the youth of the State. Since assuming office, our Government has signed seven Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) worth Rs.35,062 crore, with the potential to create 14,790 direct and indirect employment opportunit ies. 77. To encourage large -scale investments and accelerate industrial growth in Tamil Nadu, this Government will strive to set up more Multi Modal Logistics Parks (MMLPs) and Dry Ports at strategic locations , and to establish petrochemical and ancillary indu stries. This Government will also explore the possibility of setting up new ports in Tamil Nadu. 78. Tamil Nadu, one of the leading States in industrial and economic growth, will release a 40 new Tamil Nadu Industrial Policy to further strengthen this position. This Policy will foster innovation and technology -driven growth, support emerging industry sectors, and drive sustainable development and export promotion. The Government will also create the Tamil Nadu Industrial Capability Directory , a comprehensive digital platform listing the State's manufacturing and supply capabilities, enabling investors to understand the depth of the local ecosystem. 79. To further enhance Tamil Nadu's competitiveness, the Government will introduce an Artificial Intelligence (AI) -powered investment service system called 'Guidance 3.0' , making all requisite information, clearances and services available seamlessly on a single platform for companies seeking to invest in Tamil Nadu.

items.text: To further enhance Tamil Nadu's competitiveness, the Government will introduce an Artificial Intelligence (AI) -powered investment service system called 'Guidance 3.0' , making all requisite information, clearances and services available seamlessly on a single platform for companies seeking to invest in Tamil Nadu. As a key componen t of this initiative, the 'Tamil Nadu Single Window Portal 3.0' will be implemented in an upgraded form, enabling all statutory approvals, clearances and no -objection certificates required for establishing industries and investment projects to be obtain ed through a unified interface. This will make setting up of industries and investing in Tamil Nadu remarkably seamless, paving the way to 41 attract new investment and accelerate industrial growth. 80. The global Tamil diaspora, with its long-standing ties to Tamil Nadu, holds immense potential in talent, investment and entrepreneurship. To channel this goodwill into productive investment, a 'Non-Resident Tamil Investment Facilitation Desk' will be established within Guidance, to facilitate and promote investm ent by the global Tamil diaspora in the State. 81. With the objective of ensuring balanced and equitable industrial development across all regions of Tamil Nadu, SIPCOT will establish new industrial parks in industrially backward districts, based on district -specific industrial development plans and each district's sectoral strengths. These parks will be developed with state -of-the-art infrastructure suited to investors' needs, at an estimated cost of approximately Rs.3,200 crore over the next five years. 82.

items.text: These parks will be developed with state -of-the-art infrastructure suited to investors' needs, at an estimated cost of approximately Rs.3,200 crore over the next five years. 82. Thoot hukudi and Tirunelveli, in southern Tamil Nadu, will be declared as a 'Space Industrial Investment Zone' , anchored by the strategic significance of the spaceport at Kulasekarapattinam. This is expected to bring about a major leap in the 42 industrial growth o f the southern region . To provide unparalleled infrastructure and technological support to private enterprises, startups and research organisations within this zone, the State Government, in collaboration with IN -SPACe, is establishing an advanced 'Space V ehicle Common Technical Facility' . 83. India's first dedicated AI and Innovation city, named 'Arivagam' , will be established for Artificial Intelligence and deep tech development, with facilities including an AI university, an international skill development centre, a semiconductor hardware testing lab, multi -domain innovation incubators and modern residential infrastructure. It will serve as a dedicated ecosystem bringing together AI companies, deep-tech startups, quantum technology ventures, enterprise capab ility centres, research institutions and Government AI initiatives, equipped with advanced compute infrastructure, specialised facilities, a skilled workforce, and a collaborative innovation environment. Artisan communities and talented students in rural areas across Tamil Nadu also face significant challenges in accessing premier n ational -level design institutions, owing to limited opportunities, financial constraints, and lack of access to specialised educational avenues.

items.text: Artisan communities and talented students in rural areas across Tamil Nadu also face significant challenges in accessing premier n ational -level design institutions, owing to limited opportunities, financial constraints, and lack of access to specialised educational avenues. To bridge these gaps, with the active participation of industry and academia, the 'Tamil Nadu Institute of Desi gn' will be established as an institution of State importance. This institute will be established at an estimated cost of Rs.60 crore . A detailed project report for its establishment will be prepared. 89. Technical textiles is currently one of the emerging sec tors, offering opportunities for innovation, value addition, exports, and high -skilled employment across fields including healthcare, automotive, construction, agriculture and defence. Although Tamil Nadu is one of India's leading textile - producing States, this sector's contribution to overall 45 textile production remains low, owing to limited awareness of technical textiles and challenges in accessing international expertise and advanced technologies. To bridge this gap, the Technical Textiles Transformation Scheme for Entrepreneurs will be implemented in collaboration with international educational and research institutions , with the financial assistance from Tami Nadu Technical Textiles Mission. Through this scheme, entrepreneurs, Micro, Small and Medium En terprises (MSMEs), and textile manufacturers will receive international exposure, technical training, technology transfer, market intelligence, innovation support and business mentorship to facilitate their transition into the technical textiles sector. 90. The 'Tamil Nadu Palmyra Development Corporation ' will be established with an allocation of Rs.16 crore this financial year.

items.text: 90. The 'Tamil Nadu Palmyra Development Corporation ' will be established with an allocation of Rs.16 crore this financial year. items.text: 94. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is no longer a futuristic concept but a driving force improving the everyday lives of our citizens. items.text: This Government is committed to expediting the Udangudi Stage -I and Ennore SEZ Thermal Power Projects, which will together add 2,640 MW to Tamil Nadu's power generation capacity. The Vellimal ai Pumped Storage Hydroelectric Project, valued at Rs.5,050 crore, will also be expedited. The Government is actively implementing its energy strategy with a focus on renewable energy. A new 'Rooftop Solar Subsidy Scheme' will be introduced in convergence with the 'Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana'. Under this scheme, a subsidy of up to Rs.1 lakh will be provided to domestic consumers for installing solar panels, significantly reducing their electricity bills and supporting the 49 transition to renewabl e energy. An amount of Rs.50 crore is allocated to implement this scheme. A system for installing smart meters will also be introduced for all consumers in Chennai city, as well as for 50 lakh industrial and commercial consumers across other parts of the State. 99. items.text: 99. Tamil Nadu's peak power demand is projected to surpass 37,000 MW by 2035 -36, requiring accelerated investment in power generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure. As a major initiative to strengthen the State's transmission network, the Coimbatore -Ariyalur 765 KV Transmission Line Project will be implemented through the PPP mode at an estimated cost of Rs.4,000 crore. Ultra -high voltage power transmission capacity in Chennai and its surrounding areas will also be strengthened, at a n estimated cost of Rs.1,390 crore. The Phase -II Green Energy Corridor Project , valued at Rs.1,187 crore and crucial to evacuating renewable energy from southern Tamil Nadu, will be expedited alongside the Virudhunagar -Coimbatore 765 KV Transmission Project , valued at Rs.1,640 crore. The Government will also take steps to secure the financial assistance required for the third phase of the Green Energy 50 Corridor project, valued at Rs.6,884 crore, capable of handling 11,760 MW of renewable energy. 100. The next chapter of the State's growth journey will begin in the urban areas of Tamil Nadu. I am pleased to announce the 'Chief Minister's 54 Integrated Urban Development Mission' , bringing under one roof urban infrastructure, water supply, underground sewerage systems, integrated solid waste management, city roads, urban transport, expansion of green spaces, protection of urban water bodies, social infrastructure, the safe ty of women and children, AI -driven e -governance, and a dedicated Urban Public Health Improvement Mission, with the objective of addressing gaps in urban infrastructure and delivering a visibly better quality of life to every citizen of our urban local bod ies. By 2031, this Mission will reshape the urban landscape, character and functioning of Tamil Nadu's cities, positioning the State as a national role model in urban governance. An amount of Rs.2,117 crore has been allocated for this Mission in the curren t financial year. 108. The Greater Chennai Corporation serves 91 lakh people, ensuring the provision of basic facilities and creating infrastructure that improves the quality of life in the city. items.text: To improve urban transport, the Intelligent Transport Management System of Greater Chennai Corporation, developed in coordination with the Chennai City Police and the Metropolitan Transport Corporation, is in its final stage of implementation. A comprehensive street redesign and urban mobility project will also be impl emented, 55 with key emphasis on pedestrian infrastructure, accessibility for all, and urban design enhancements, including smart parking management at 20 locations and the restructuring of roads in the Ambattur and Guindy industrial estates. To expand Chenna i's green canopy and create people -centric public spaces, footpaths along major routes and residential zones will also undergo greening and beautification. 109. As part of the vision to transform Chennai into a sustainable and disaster -resilient city, blue-green infrastructure projects will be undertaken around water bodies across the city. The height of retaining walls is being raised and chain -link fences erected to expand their discharge capacity and mitigate urban flooding, protecting environmental resource s while creating sustainable spaces for community use. 110. The Ring Main Pipeline system, connecting all major drinking water sources in Chennai with drinking water distribution stations, is being undertaken at an estimated cost of Rs.3,108 crore, and is expe cted to be completed within 2030-31. This project will secure a reliable, equitable, and round -the-clock drinking water supply across Chennai city. This is the most fundamental promise 56 every great city makes to its people: clean drinking water, without exc eption, every single day . 111.

items.text: This project will secure a reliable, equitable, and round -the-clock drinking water supply across Chennai city. People -friendly streets will be developed in all municipal corporations, transforming them into modern urban thoroughfares with proper road connectivity, dedicated pedestrian pathways, separate cycling lanes, well -connected cross -streets, junction improvements, safe school access networks, and modern LED street lighting. 112. Our historic city of Chennai is one in which many of us were born and raised, a city that has embraced us and become an inseparable part of who we are. It grieves many of us that the Adyar and the Cooum, rivers that once met the drinking -water needs of the city, have today been reduced to little more than channels of sewage. Successive Governments that held office in the past squandered several hundred crores of the people's tax money in the name of cleansing and beautifying the Adyar and the Cooum, yet no meaningful change was ever brought in the condition of these rivers. The greatest and most ancient civilisations of the world, Harappa, Mohenjo -daro, the Inca, an d Mesopotamia, all flourished upon the banks of great rivers. The Government led by our Hon'ble Chief Minister 57 will strive with the utmost resolve to restore the Cooum and the Adyar to their natural state. Rivers such as the Cheonggyecheon in Seoul and th e Kallang in Singapore have, through river rejuvenation, become identities spoken of the world over.

items.text: Water Resources 122. The Government of Tamil Nadu will continue to safeguard the State's rightful share of inter -state river waters , its interests and rights in water sharing. Tamil Nadu Government will ensure timely Cauvery water releases in accordance 61 with established agreements, tribunal awards and judicial directions. Tamil Nadu's wate r rights will be protected through sustained legal, technical and administrative efforts, including opposition to projects that may affect the State's entitlements, such as the Mekedatu Project, and the State's interests in inter -state river water sharin g will be fully safeguarded. The Government will also pursue the raising of the Mullai Periyar Dam water level, implementation of the Anaimalaiyar and Nallar dam projects, and the early execution of the Godavari -Cauvery River Link Project, to strengthen long-term water security and support farmers' welfare. 123. Water sources are the lifeline of agriculture, yet various river interlinking projects announced by previous Governments have progressed at a slow pace, affecting agricultural productivity growth . Recognising this, this Government will take steps to expedite such river interlinking initiatives. The Cauvery -Vaigai -Gundar River Linking Project, will commence in this year with an initial allocation of Rs.150 crore. Further, an allocation of Rs.50 crore has been provided for preparing Detailed Project Reports for the Pennaiyar -Cheyyar, Pennaiyar -Palar, and Tamirabarani -Vaippar river linking projects. 62 Accordingly, a total allocation of Rs.200 crore has been made for the implementation and planning of these river -linking initiatives. 124.

items.text: 62 Accordingly, a total allocation of Rs.200 crore has been made for the implementation and planning of these river -linking initiatives. 124. It is a matter of grave concern that the lifelines of Tamil Nadu, the great rivers of Cauvery, Vaigai and Tamiraparani, have been continuously polluted due to direct discharge of untreated industrial effluents, domestic sewage and dumping of solid waste on river banks, resulting in severe pollution in stretches passing through industrialised and urbanised areas. To restore the purity of these rivers, this Government will conduct detailed feasibilit y studies and prepare Detailed Project Report s covering the installation of sewerage and effluent treatment plants for liquid waste, comprehensive solid waste management in rural and urban areas along these rivers, riverfront development in urban areas and river surface cleaning. An amo unt of Rs.25 crore is being allocated for the preliminary and feasibility study for this project. 125. To ensure groundwater recharge, availability of fresh water for irrigation and conservation of water during the monsoon, this Government will conduct detailed feasibility study for the Construction of Barrages across the River 63 Cauvery , with an allocation of Rs.10 crore for the feasibility study and project report. The Government envi sions a rural Tamil Nadu with digitally empowered local bodies that build self-reliant and resilient communities, sustainable infrastructure that supports growth, and rising living standards that ultimately eradicate rural poverty to ensure a dignified liv elihood for every family. 131. The foremost among the challenges prioritized by this Government is to ensure permanent 65 housing to homeless poor families in rural areas. Even though several housing schemes have been implemented by the State and Union Governments over the past thirty years, Tamil Nadu is yet to achieve hut-free status. Insufficient funding, inclusion and exclusion errors in beneficiary identification and scarcity of lands in rural areas remain key challenges in th is sector. To gradually resolve this issue, the Government is launching a new State Housing Scheme named the 'Vetri Veedu Thittam' exclusively for Kutcha Hut dwelling families. 132. Due to the lower unit cost fixed for houses, genuine and highly deserving poor households are being excluded from housing schemes . Only families capable of bearing the additional expenses are being selected . The Government has therefore decided to increase the unit cost from Rs.3.1 lakh to Rs.5 lakh for construction of Pucca houses to those living in Kutcha huts under this new scheme. In the first year, 70,000 houses will be sanctioned at an estimated cost of Rs.3,500 crore .

The Rural Development Department has implemented a wide range of schemes over the years, 66 but overlap between these schemes and the absence of a planned approach have limited their effectiveness. To address this, the Government is integrating a ll infrastructure schemes of the Department into a comprehensive scheme, the 'Tamil Nadu Village Empowerment, Transformation, Rejuvenation Initiative' (TN -VETRI) , which will include separate sub -missions for Water Supply, Solid Waste Management, Sanitation and Rural Connectivity. 134. To strengthen basic infrastructure in Peri-urban Panchayats surrounding urban areas, an exclusive sub -scheme under TN -VETRI will be implemented with an allocation of Rs.1,000 crore. A further sub -scheme, with an annual allocation of Rs.100 crore, will support the development of Hill Area Village Panchayats. Overall, TN -VETRI will be implemented with an annual financial allocation of Rs.6,000 crore, and will also converge with the needs and resources of other departments and Govern ment of India schemes. A High -Level Committee, chaired by the Hon'ble Minister for Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, will oversee this coordination. 135. items.text: 72 Government will take further steps to advance to the next critical phase: empowering our public servants with modern tools such as AI in governance to enhance productivity and deliver seamless public services. 150. First, dismantling unnecessary centralization through the delegation of powers to the subordinates. By eliminating arbitrary bottlenecks that once bred corruption, we ensure citizen s receive their rightful approvals without delay or harassment. Second, digital workflows are being streamlined. To ensure accountability, a Quality Assurance Audit Board backed by AI will continuously monitor file flows and decision quality, eliminating u njust rejections and backlogs. Finally, we will turn technology into an ally for our employees. By integrating AI, Agentic workflows, and Speech -to-Text capabilities (Prompt), employees will get automated assistance for routine tasks such as drafting, summ arizing rules, and documentation, reducing the drudgery of manual processing, and freeing our officers to focus on informed, impactful decision -making. 151. Our goal is simple; a corruption -free, transparent, clean and highly efficient administration where tec hnology serves the public servant, and the 73 public servant serves the people in delivering services digitally, transparently in a time bound manner. To transform public service delivery and streamline administrative workflows, a Governance Processes Reforms Committee will be constituted under the chairmanship of Chief Secretary. Bringing together senior administrative leaders, industry transformation experts, and academic system designers, the Committee will re -engineer bureaucratic processes, eliminate redu ndant compliance, and build a modern, technology -enabled, citizen friendly (G2C) and business friendly (G2B) governance ecosystem in the State. 152.

items.text: 11,532 crore is being allocated for the Revenue and Disaster Management Department. Commercial Tax and Registration 156. This Government firmly believes in a fair, transparent and trust -based administration of the Goods and Services Tax, recognising honest taxpayers as true partners in the State's development. To further 75 ease their compliance burden, Commercial Taxes Department is transition ing to a service -oriented, technology -driven, faceless approach powered by non-intrusive verification. While remaining committed to supporting and simplifying compliance for honest taxpayers, firm, intelligence -led action will be strictly reserved for wilful evaders alone. 157. Recognising the vital role of the Registration Department as the public record office, our Government is undertaking landmark reforms to ensure seamless, convenient and hassle -free registration of documents. By prioritising digital innovation and civic convenience, the Government is committed to making property registration effortless and corruption -free, with the protection of innocent property buyers from fraudulent registrations being a top prio rity. Necessary amendments to Act and Rules, aligned with Supreme Court rulings and best practices across leading States, will be enacted to this end. ' Anywhere Registration ' will be a cornerstone of this reform, allowing citizens to register documents fro m the convenience of their homes. In a phased manner, the Registration Department will transition to a completely paperless and presence -less registration mode, using advanced 76 digital authentication without compromising the legal security or authenticity o f any transaction. 158. In the Revised Budget Estimates, Rs.651 crore is being allocated for the Commercial Taxes Department and Rs.475 crore is being allocated for the Stamps and Registration Department. Natural Resources 159.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister) [Finance department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister)

items.text: 158. In the Revised Budget Estimates, Rs.651 crore is being allocated for the Commercial Taxes Department and Rs.475 crore is being allocated for the Stamps and Registration Department. Natural Resources 159. This Government will take all necessary steps to prevent illegal mining and quarrying in the State and ensure that revenues due to the Government are collected without any leakage. In the last 3 months, since this Government was formed, 1,307 vehicles have been seized for illicit mineral smuggling, and 1,161 First Information Reports have been filed. In a special drive against illicit mining, 431 quarries were inspected and violations were detected in 155 cases and action is being taken against these quar ries as per law . A special task force has also been formed to inspect crushing units and stockyards across the State, and check posts have been established in border areas. 160. To further strengthen mineral management in the State, an end -to-end mineral manage ment system with real -time monitoring of mineral 77 production and movement will be established. This technology -driven, transparent and integrated framework will ensure sustainable extraction of the State's mineral wealth and optimisation of revenue while pr eventing illegal mining. District -level vigilance and enforcement wings will also be established to strengthen surveillance and prevent illegal mining. An amount of Rs.3 crore has been provided in the Revised Budget Estimates for 2026 -27 to implement this scheme. 161. Granite polishing and design centres will be established in Pudukkottai and Perambalur districts to develop the granite industry in the region. A Detailed Project Report will be prepared during the current financial year.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister) [Finance department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister)

items.text: 161. Granite polishing and design centres will be established in Pudukkottai and Perambalur districts to develop the granite industry in the region. A Detailed Project Report will be prepared during the current financial year. In the Revised Budget Est imates, Rs.438 crore is being allocated for the Natural Resources Department. Welfare of Government Employees 162. Government has launched the New Health Insurance Scheme, 2026 for Government Employees and their eligible family members, and Pensioners (including spouses) and Family Pensioners, for a period of five years from 01.07.2026 to 30.06.2031. Under the new sche me, the basic sum insured has been enhanced from Rs.5 lakh to Rs.7.50 lakh, and 78 coverage for specified illnesses has been enhanced from Rs.10 lakh to Rs.12 lakh. The Corpus Fund for rare and specified illnesses has also been enhanced from Rs.10 lakh to Rs. 15 lakh for employees. The Scheme covers 2,992 medical procedures and 46 specified illness procedures, through a network of 1,535 empanelled hospitals and Government Medical Institutions. This Government, committed to the welfare of Government employees, has allocated Rs.838 crore to implement this insurance scheme. In the Revised Budget Estimates, Rs. 47,240 crore is being allocated for Pensions and Other Retirement Benefits. Administration of Justice 163. The judiciary plays an indispensable role in upholding the rule of law and ensuring the timely delivery of justice.

items.title: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister)

items.text: In the Revised Budget Estimates, Rs. 47,240 crore is being allocated for Pensions and Other Retirement Benefits. Administration of Justice 163. The judiciary plays an indispensable role in upholding the rule of law and ensuring the timely delivery of justice. Recognising the need for modern court infrastructure to serve the public, our Government will revive the proposal for establish ing an Integrated Court Complex at Broadway, Chennai, combining 160 courts, at an estimated cost of Rs.1,375 crore. A sum of Rs.10 crore is being allocated for undertaking the preliminary steps for this project. In the Revised Budget Estimates, Rs.2,486 crore is being allocated for the Administration of Justice Depar tment. 79 Tourism 164. Tamil Nadu ’s rich heritage, vibrant culture, and diverse landscapes make tourism a vital driver of economic growth, employment generation, and local empowerment. Investing in tourism strengthens local livelihoods, preserves our cultural identity, and accelerates state wide infrastructure development. 165. To ensure a reliable, long -term financing mechanism for scaling up tourism infrastructure, this Government proposes to create a dedicated Sustainable Tourism Development Fund. A Bill to estab lish this statutory fund will be introduced in the present Assembly session to enable seamless mobilization of resources, catalyze private investments, and secure sustained funding for future tourism initiatives across the State. 166. Under our vision to elevat e iconic landmarks to international standards, the Government will comprehensively develop Mahabalipuram into a global tourism destination. To realize this vision, we are submitting a detailed proposal to the Government of India under its scheme for iconic destination development to secure a central grant of Rs.200 crore.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister) [Finance department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister)

items.text: To realize this vision, we are submitting a detailed proposal to the Government of India under its scheme for iconic destination development to secure a central grant of Rs.200 crore. This strategic investment will upgrade world -class 80 visitor amenities, enhance connectivity, and cement Tamil Nadu ’s position on the global tourism map. 167. To promote river tourism across Tamil Nadu, an allocation of Rs.53 crore is being made to develop key riverfronts across three major rivers: along the Kaveri River from Hogenakkal to Srirangam, along the Vaigai River in Madurai, and along the Thamirabarani River from Papanasam to Ti runelveli. Additionally, to popularize the rich culinary and artistic heritage of our state, this Government will implement a project to highlight local food tourism routes through dedicated Food and Arts Festivals, supported by an allocation of Rs.20 crore. 168. Demonstrating our commitment to social welfare and spiritual tourism, senior citizens will be enabled to visit their chosen holy pilgrimage sites every year with fully sponsored air -conditioned travel, comfortable lodging, and quality meals, funded by an allocation of Rs.20 crore in Tamil Nadu . Furthermore, to cater to the growing influx of devotees, modern rest houses will be established at Thirukkadaiyur, Nagore, and Velankanni at an estimated cost of Rs.60 crore, ensuring safe and comforta ble accommodation for all pilgrims 81 169. Government will launch 'Tamil Nadu Eco-Tourism Mission' to develop and expand nature -based tourism circuits and destinations, including trekking routes, wildlife safaris, birding and boating trails, eco -friendly stays, and interpretation and visitor centres.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister) [Finance department]

items.text: Government will launch 'Tamil Nadu Eco-Tourism Mission' to develop and expand nature -based tourism circuits and destinations, including trekking routes, wildlife safaris, birding and boating trails, eco -friendly stays, and interpretation and visitor centres. Th is Mission will be implemented across the State's diverse landscapes, including forest and wildlife areas, through active community participation, enhancing livelihood opportunities for local and tribal communities while contributing to forest conservation and fostering nature awareness among the public. An amount of Rs.25 crore has been allocated for this scheme. Art & Culture 170. Tamil heritage and cultural sites along the East Coast Road will be upgraded to showcase and preserve the unique history and rich heritage of Tamil people . An amount of Rs.5 crore is being allocated for the preparation of Detailed Project Report in the Revised Budget Estimates 2026 -27. 171. This Government will introduce a ‘Folk Artists Livelihood Protection Scheme ’, under which 200 best -performing art troupes registered with the Folk Artists Welfare Board will be selected each year, providing them opportunities to perform for 82 100 days. A sum of Rs.23 crore is being allocated for this scheme. In the Revised Budget E stimates, Rs.775 crore is being allocated for the Tourism, Art and Culture Department. Tamil Development 172. Our Government remains steadfast in its commitment to preserving Tamil heritage, and encouraging young talent. To foster early appreciation of cl assical literature, Government is instituting an incentive award of Rs.5,000 each for 500 primary school students (up to Class 5) who memorize and recite 300 Thirukkural couplets.

items.text: To foster early appreciation of cl assical literature, Government is instituting an incentive award of Rs.5,000 each for 500 primary school students (up to Class 5) who memorize and recite 300 Thirukkural couplets. Government is also enhancing financial support for Tamil scholars and organizing state -wide essay and elocution competitions for college students to commemorate the sacrifices of our Tamil language martyrs. 173. Furthermore, to honour the legendary legacy of Quaid -e-Millat, a new award celebrating his deep love for the Tami l language will be presented annually on Thiruvalluvar Thirunaal. 174. Further, through the Tamil Virtual Academy, a Tamil Large Language Model (Tamil LLM) will be developed, AI -based language 83 technology tools will be deployed for official Government communications, and, in collaboration with leading universities, a dedicated Artificial Intelligence model for Tamil will be developed. 175. Tamil Nadu has world -renowned archaeological sites and a cultural history and urban civilisation spanning thousands of years. With the objective of ensuring that students acquire both academic and field knowledge, school students will be taken on visits to the archaeological and heritage sites across Tamil Nadu — including Keeladi, Adichanallur, Kodumanal, Mayiladumparai, Sivakalai, Alagankulam, Arikamedu, Saluvankuppam, an d Kaveripattinam — promoting experiential learning and strengthening their understanding of the State's ancient history, civilisation and cultural heritage. For this purpose, the Government allocates R s.One crore to organise educational tours for school st udents to archaeological sites and institutions of higher education.

items.text: For this purpose, the Government allocates R s.One crore to organise educational tours for school st udents to archaeological sites and institutions of higher education. Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department 176. Over the next five years, this Government plans to undertake renovation works and perform Thirukudamuzhukku (Consecration) at 3,000 te mples, restore 250 temple tanks, and repair 75 wooden 84 temple cars. The Government also plans to upgrade basic amenities at temples receiving large numbers of devotees, providing safe drinking water, restrooms, bathrooms, accommodation and other essential infrastructure. Recognising the need to appoint Trustees to temples, this Government, immediately after assuming office, issued notifications for the appointment of Trustees to 9,205 temples within a short span, and action is underway to complete these appointments. With a budgetary allocation of Rs.418 crore, restoration and conservation works are also being carried out at 213 temples that are over a thousand years old. Alongside various structural reforms in the Department, the Government is paying focus ed attention to safeguarding the movable and immovable properties of temples. In the Revised Budget Estimates, Rs.708 crore is being allocated for the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department. 85 PART B Finances of the State Government Hon’ble Speaker, 177. In my speech so far, I have highlighted the major Schemes of this Government. 178.

items.text: In the Revised Budget Estimates, Rs.708 crore is being allocated for the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department. 85 PART B Finances of the State Government Hon’ble Speaker, 177. In my speech so far, I have highlighted the major Schemes of this Government. 178. Finally, I must state that this Government had presented the White paper on States finances last month on 16 th June, 2026, clearly and faithfully bringing out the real fiscal position of the State and the financial distress that has resulted out of poor administration and leakages in the revenue collecting departments and undertaking expenditures culminating in ve ry high borrowing by State Government and its parastatal companies, namely, TNEB ’s successor companies, TNCSC and State Transport Undertakings. The State has been borrowing without reference to what the revenues can sustain. While there is nothing wrong in borrowing for investing in human and physical capital in the State that act as drivers of economic and social growth, this needs to be accompanied by 86 corresponding efforts in mobilisation of resources that could cover borrowings. Previous government fail ed to see this simple fact. 179. It let the revenue earning departments to uncontrollably bleed, while letting a good share of public money in works to be extracted out by unscrupulous middlemen. Since, the formation of our Government under the leadership of the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, we have made continuous efforts to plug leakages in both revenue and expenditure side, enabling the State Government to create at least Rs.1,500 cr ore on the revenue side so far, and we expect large fiscal space cr eation on the expenditure side, due to savings in the cost of procurement of goods and services.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister) [Finance department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister)

items.text: 180. I must also reiterate what I said during my presentation of the White Paper that this Government under the visionary leadership of our Honourable Chief Ministe r, believes that the welfare schemes such as scholarships and free education to students, subsidies to our entrepreneurs to commence business and 87 manufacturing, PDS subsidies, free housing for the poor, etc are not largesse, but are investments in human an d social capital that drives consumption and growth in the economy in the long run. In fact, this Government is continuing most of the schemes for public welfare that has been in existence for the last three decades and plans to expand them further. Howe ver, a calibrated balance between welfare scheme investments in human capital and investments in physical capital and infrastructure is necessary. These however require resources and fiscal space, and without sustained effort by the Government in this reg ard, it is impossible to sustain welfare schemes. 181. As I have already mentioned earlier, this Government has already taken action towards mobilization of nearly Rs.15,000 crore through various measures and has also constituted a high level Revenue Augmenta tion Committee under the chairman ship of renowned economist Thiru. Montek Singh Ahluwalia. We will also constitute a similar high level Expenditure Reforms Committee to advise the State Government on rationalising 88 expenditure by enhancing the productivit y of the service delivery apparatus of the State and reviewing all welfare schemes by evaluating their positive impact on the target beneficiary groups and ensuring that all people who need State intervention truly benefit.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister) [Finance department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Budget Speech 2026-27 (Finance Minister)

items.text: I must clarify here that the sc ope of the Committee would not be restricted to reducing expenditure, but to rationalising them, which would also include expanding welfare schemes that have good positive externalities and benefits to the society and the State in the long run. 182. The fiscal position of the State is in the red, and we have been handed a treasury box that is overburdened with debt and sub optimal income with leaking holes. The repair has been started, but would need at least two years to bring the financial administration back to the track of fiscal prudence. Under the leadership of our Honourable Chief Minister, we have been successful in all our previous ventures in political landscape, and we will attain “Vetri ” in this venture also. Tamil Nadu will emerge as a State that has fiscally prudent governance for balanced and inclusive economic 89 growth. Unlike the previous government, which focussed only on short term political gains with the belief that they should make best use of their five year term, our Government believes t hat we need to look forward to at least 15 years of sustained growth through consistent policies and providing clean and efficient governance. 183. In the Revised Budget Estimates (RBE) 2026–27, SOTR is estimated at Rs.2,26,740 crore, compared to the Interim Budget Estimates (IBE) 2026–27 projection of Rs.2,29,579 crore. This allocation includes Rs.1,56,176 crore for Commercial Taxes, Rs.35,109 crore for Stamps and Registration, Rs.14,861 crore for Motor Vehicle Taxes, and Rs.14,164 crore for State Excise.

items.text: This allocation includes Rs.1,56,176 crore for Commercial Taxes, Rs.35,109 crore for Stamps and Registration, Rs.14,861 crore for Motor Vehicle Taxes, and Rs.14,164 crore for State Excise. Al igning with the observations in the White Paper on Fiscal Management regarding past over - estimations, projections have been recalibrated downward in the Revised Budget Estimates. State ’s Own Tax Revenue is projected to expand at a growth rate of 9.78 per c ent in 2026–27 over the Revised Estimates (RE) of 2025–26. 90 184. The State ’s Own Non -Tax Revenue is estimated at Rs.27,704 crore in Interim Budget Estimates, as compared to Rs.26,265 crore in the Revised Estimates 2025 -26. The Grants -in-aid receivable from the Union Government were estimated at Rs.24,762 crore in Interim Budget Estimates 2026-27. The Union Government has introduced a new scheme, ‘Viksit Bharat -Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) in place of the Mahatma Gand hi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme. An amount of Rs.7,586 crore has been provided under this scheme with a 60:40 sharing pattern.

Furthermore, a sum of Rs.3,461 crore that is due to be released to Tamil Nadu under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme has also been included in the Revised Budget Estimates for the 91 year 2026 -27. Now in Revised Budget Estimate Grants -in-aid from Centre is estimated at Rs.32,922 crore . 186. The share in central taxes was estimated at Rs.56,819 crore in the Revised Estimates 2025 -26. The same was estimated at Rs.62,531 crore in the Interim Budget Estimates 2026-27, based on the Union Government ’s allocation in their Budget. The same is retai ned in Revised Budget Estimate 2026 -27. 187. In aggregate, the Total Revenue Receipts projected to be Rs.3,09,698 crore in the Revised Estimates 2025 -26 and projected at Rs.3,44,575 crore in the Interim Budget Estimates 2026-27, has now been estimated at Rs.3, 50,027 crore in the Revised Budget Estimates 2026-27. This is Rs.5,452 crore increase over the Interim Budget Estimates. 188. items.text: 188. On the expenditure front, Total Revenue Expenditure is revised upward to Rs.4,05,802 crore in Revised Budget Estimates 2026–27 from R s.3,93,272 crore in Interim Budget 92 Estimates 2026–27. This increase is attributable to mandatory outlays for new flagship commitments, agricultural crop loan waivers, 200 units of free electricity, and the Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram scheme. 189. The overall Cap ital Expenditure in the Interim Budget Estimates 2026 -27 projected at Rs.59,562 crore, is estimated at Rs.56,985 crore in the Revised Budget Estimates 2026 -27. The total capital outlay of the State including Net Loans and Advances is estimated at Rs.66,0 60 crore in the Revised Budget Estimates 2026-27. 190. The Revenue Deficit in the Interim Budget Estimates 2026 -27 was Rs.48,696 crore. It is pertinent to note that this is an underestimate particularly by means of over estimation of Revenue Receipts and lesse r estimate of Revenue Expenditure. Hence, the Revenue Deficit is estimated to increase to Rs.55,775 crore in Revised Budget Estimates 2026 -27. 93 191. The Fiscal Deficit in Revised Budget Estimates 2026 -27 is estimated at Rs.1,21,819 crore as against Rs.1,21,949 crore in Interim Budget Estimates 2026 -27. The Fiscal Deficit is within the targets fixed under Tamil Nadu Fiscal Responsibility Act 2003. 192.

items.text: The Fiscal Deficit is within the targets fixed under Tamil Nadu Fiscal Responsibility Act 2003. 192. The Overall Outstanding liability of the State is estimated to be Rs.10,98,768 crore in the Revised Budget Estimates 2026-27 as against Rs.10,99,458 crore in the Interim Budget Estimates 2026 -27. The outstanding liability includes Public Debt and the Public Account Liability of the State. It may be noted that the Public Debt includes an amount of Rs.9,523 crore which sho uld reflect in the accounts of the Union Government after the approval of Chennai Metro Rail Phase – II project as a Central Sector Project. As and when the necessary book adjustments are made by the Government of India, the public Debt will reduce to that extent. 193. The Outstanding Debt., that is, the overall liability to GSDP ratio in Revised Budget Estimates 2026 -27 is estimated at 27.01 per cent 94 as compared to 27.03 per cent in the Interim Budget Estimates 2026 -27. Hon’ble Speaker Sir, 194. This Government will take firm steps towards achieving growth in revenue by sealing the leakages in tax collection, increasing the collection efficiency and through taking revenue augmentation measures. The Government will strive to receive the optimum level of Grants in aid receivable from the Union Government eligible to the State. Through these measures, the Revenue and Fiscal Deficit are expected to decrease in the forthcoming years. This will consequently lead to boosting of Capital Expenditure and achieving the desirable growth. 195. Tamil Nadu possesses the economic strength, the institutional depth, and the human resources to restore its fiscal health.
