items.text: குறு, சிறு மற்றும் நடுத்தரத் ததொழில் நிறுவனங்கள் – திறன் பயிற்சி மற்றும் வவலைவொய்ப்புத் திட்டம் 1. திட்டத்திலன தெயல்படுத்தும் அலமப்பு எது? மொநிை அளவில் ததொழில் வணிகத்துலற ஆலையரகமும், தென்லன மொவட்டத்திற்கு மண்டை இலை இயக்குநர் தென்லன அவர்களும் மற்றும் இதர மொவட்டங்களுக்கு தபொது வமைொளர்கள் மொவட்ட ததொழில் லமயமும் தெயல்படுத்தும் நிறுவனங்கள் ஆகும். 2. திட்டத்தின் கீழ் பயிற்சி தபறுதற்கொன தகுதிகள் யொலவ? விண்ைப்பதொரர்கள் வதசிய திறன் வமம்பொட்டு க் கழகங்கள் / வதசிய திறன் வமம்பொட்டு முகவர்கள் மற்றும் அலதப்வபொன்ற நிறுவனங்களின் நிபந்தலனகளுக்கு உட்பட்டு வதலவயொன கல்வி தகுதி மற்றும் வயது வரம்லப பூர்த்தி தெய்பவரொக இருத்தல் வவண்டும். விண்ைப்பதொரர் கடந்த மூன்றொண்டுகள் ததொடர்ச்சியொக தமிழ் நொட்டில் வசிப்பவரொக இருத்தல் வவண்டும். இத்திட்டத்தின் கீழ் தபொறியியல், பட்டம் அல்ைது பட்டயம் அல்ைது ததொழில் பயிற்சி நிறுவனத்தில் படித்த 18 -45 வயதிற்குட்பட்ட வவலைவொய்ப்பற்ற இலளஞர்களுக்கு பயிற்சியுடன் கூடிய வவலை வொய்ப்பு வழங்கப்படும். 3. திட்டத்லதச் தெயல்படுத்துவதற்கொன நிதி எவ்வொறு தபறப்படுகிறது? திட்டத்லதச் தெயல்படுத்துவதற்கொன முழு நிதியும் தமிழ்நொடு மொநிை அரெொல் தமிழ்நொடு திறொன் வமம்பொட்டுக் கழகம் மூைமொக வழங்கப்படுகிறது. 4. இத்திட்டத்தின் கீழ் குறு சிறு மற்றும் நடுத்தர த் ததொழில் நிறுவனங்களின் ப ங்கு யொது? குறு சிறு மற்றும் நடுத்தர த் ததொழில் நிறுவனங்கள் திறன் பயிற்சி ெொன்றிதழ்களுடன் கூடிய வவலைவொய்ப்பிலன வழங்கும். குறு சிறு மற்றும் நடுத்தர த் ததொழில் நிறுவனங்கள், பயிற்சி அளி ப்பதற்குத் வதலவயொன தகு திகள் பயிற்சியொளர்களுக்கு இருத்தலை உறுதி தெய்ய வவண்டும்.

items.text: 5. பயிற்சியின் வபொது வழங்கப்படும் உதவித்ததொலக எவ்வளவு? இத்திட்டத்தின்படி குறு சிறு மற்றும் நடுத்தரத் ததொழில் நிறுவனங்கள் வதலவயொன திறன் பயிற்சியிலன தகுதி வொய்ந்த இலளஞர்களுக்கு 6 மொத கொைத்திற்கு வழங்கும் இக்கொைத்தில் குலறந்தபட்ெ ஊதியமொக மொதத்திற் கு ரூ.5000/ - வீதம் பயிற்சி அளிக்கும் நிறுவனங்களொல் பயிற்சி தபறுபவர்களுக்கு வழங்கப்படும். அத்ததொழில் பயிற்சி கொைத்திற்கு அரசு மொதொந்திரமொக ரூ.2000/ - வீதம் 6 மொத கொைத்திற்கு பயிற்சி ஊக்கத்ததொலகலய அளிக்கும். 6. தமிழ்நொட்டுக்கு தவளிவய வசிப்பவர் இத்திட்டத்தின் கீழ் பயிற்சி தபற விண்ைப்பிக்க இயலுமொ? இயைொது. விண்ைப்பதொரர் கடந்த மூன்றொண்டுகள் ததொடர்ச்சியொக தமிழ் நொட்டில் வசிப்பவரொக இருத்தல் வவண்டும்.

items.text: ABSTRACT Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Department -Schemes - Implementation of Tamil Nadu Women Entrepreneur Empowerment Scheme (TWEES) from the year 2025-2026 onwards - Necessary modalities / guidelines for implementation of the scheme and sanction of funds - Orders - Issued. Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (D2) Department G.O. (Ms.) No.51 Dated: 25.08.2025 திருவள்ளுவர்‌ ஆண்டு 2056 விசுவாவசு வருடம்‌, ஆவணி- 9 Read: 1. Announcement made by Hon’ble Minister (Finance, Environment & Climate Change) during the Budget Speech 2025-2026 on 14.03.2025. 2. From the Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce, Guindy, Chennai-32, letter Rc.No. 10730/DIC2/2025 dated: 09.05.2025. ORDER: The Hon'ble Minister for Finance, Environment and Climate Change during the Budget Speech 2025-2026(para 248) has made the following announcement: - துமிழற்நாட்டின்‌ பொருளாதார வளர்ச்சியில்‌ பெண்களின்‌ பங்கு மேலும்‌ அதிகறிக்க வேண்டும்‌ என்ற நோக்கத்துடன்‌; அடுத்து வரும்‌ ஐந்து ஆண்டுகளில்‌ ஒரு இலட்சம்‌ மகளிரை தொழில்‌ முனைவோராக உயர்த்திடும்‌ பெருந்திட்டம்‌ ஒன்று செயல்படுத்தப்படும்‌. இத்திட்டத்தின்‌ கீழ்‌ 20 சதல$தமானியத்துடன்‌ [unclear figure] இலட்சம்‌ ரூப௱ப்‌ வரை வங்கிக்கடன்‌ பெற்று, மகஸிர்‌ பல்வேறு தெ௱றில்கள்‌ தொடங்கிட அரிய திறன்‌ மேம்பாட்டுப்‌ பயிற்சிகள்‌, 2ிற்பனைக்கான ஆலேோசனைகரும்‌ அழங்கப்படும்‌.

items.text: 2025-2026 ஆம்‌ ஆண்டில்‌ அத்திட்டத்திற்கான மானிய நிதி/க.விக்கென 225 கேடி ரூப௱ப்‌ ஒதுக்கப்படும்‌. ” 2. Based on the above announcement, the _ Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce in the letter second read above has submitted the following proposal: - (i) There is a growing need to create a robust avenue for women entrepreneurs, especially from economically and socially disadvantaged backgrounds among the 1.77 Crore women in the age group of 18 to 49 years. (P.T.O) fag (ii) In line with the above, this initiative will not only uplift women financially but also contribute to the State's MSME growth, employment generation, and inclusive economic development. The primary target group comprises aspiring women aged between 18 and 55 years who are interested in pursuing entrepreneurship. This includes women from diverse educational and socio-economic backgrounds who possess the ambition, drive, or potential to start, manage, or scale their own businesses. (iii) The scheme is intended to support one lakh women across the State over five years to become self employed by setting up of new Manufacturing or Service or Trading enterprises by availing loan upto a maximum of Rs. 10lakh, with subsidy assistance from the State Government @20% of the project cost and 6% Interest subvention on the loan component. This will also match the quantum of assistance being provided in other existing schemes implemented by the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Department. (iv)To encourage and facilitate women empowerment through entrepreneurship, an exclusive entrepreneurship development scheme with the following key Components is formulated. (a) Entrepreneurship Development and skill training (b) Entrepreneurial Mentorship & Handholding Support.

items.text: (iv)To encourage and facilitate women empowerment through entrepreneurship, an exclusive entrepreneurship development scheme with the following key Components is formulated. (a) Entrepreneurship Development and skill training (b) Entrepreneurial Mentorship & Handholding Support. (c) Financial Assistance (v) To approve the proposed draft guidelines for implementation of “Tamil Nadu Women Entrepreneurs Empowerment Scheme (TWEES)”. (vi) (a) An allocation of Rs.225 crore is provided only for Individual Based subsidy in the Budget Estimate for the year 2025-2026 under the Individual Based Subsidy Head of Account. b) Budgetary Allocation Plan for the Inception year 2025-2026:- உ Individual based Subsidy covers the largest share, allowing support for women with varied enterprise sizes upto the project cost of Rs.10.00 lakh. e Training, handholding and mentorship includes entrepreneurship and skill, business planning, legal literacy, marketing, digital tools, etc,. -3- e Scheme Advertisement & Publicity covers the promotion and awareness activities related to the scheme. This includes the preparation and dissemination of brochures, pamphlets, banners, posters, media advertisements (print, electronic, and_ social media), organizing awareness camps, workshops, and other outreach initiatives aimed at informing and educating potential beneficiaries about the scheme and its benefits. (vii) By enabling women to start or scale their businesses, this initiative is expected to contribute to employment generation, economic independence for women, and overall socio-economic development in the region.

items.text: (vii) By enabling women to start or scale their businesses, this initiative is expected to contribute to employment generation, economic independence for women, and overall socio-economic development in the region. It will enable the establishment of at least 1,00,000 new women- led micro and small enterprises across diverse sectors such as manufacturing, services, food processing, retail, textiles, Agro-based industries, etc. Each enterprise is expected to employ 2 to 5 persons, resulting in approximately 3 lakh new employment opportunities, with a strong focus on local and rural job creation. Strengthen the entrepreneurial ecosystem through targeted skill development, financial access, mentoring, and support services for women. Boost the participation of women in the state’s Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises sector. Facilitate access to institutional credit for over 1 lakh women, improving their formal credit history and banking relationships. Promote financial literacy and digital payment adoption among women entrepreneurs. The dual objective of financial and social upliftment of women is central to the mission of empowering aspiring women entrepreneurs. 3. In view of the above, the Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce has requested the Government to issue necessary orders for implementing the above scheme. 4.

In view of the above, the Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce has requested the Government to issue necessary orders for implementing the above scheme. 4. The Government carefully examined the proposal of the Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce and issue the following orders: - (a) Administrative sanction is accorded to implement the scheme called “Tamil Nadu Women Entrepreneur Empowerment Scheme (TWEES)’and financial sanction is accorded for utilizing the fund of Rs.225.00 Crore provided in BE 2025-2026 to meet out the expenditure towards various components of the scheme from the year 2025-2026 Onwards. -4- (b) The guidelines as detailed in Annexure-I & II to this order are approved for the implementation of “Tamil Nadu Women Entrepreneur Empowerment Scheme (TWEES)”. (c) The Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce is permitted to issue directives to the Task Force Committee concerning projects falling under the Focus/Priority Sectors. (d) The Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce is authorized to engage PMUs through FaMeTN at the Commissionerate of Industries and Commerce and at the districts for monitoring and reporting the performance of the scheme and also permitted to incur the expenditure towards PMUs to be met out from the funds of FaMe TN. (e) The Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce is authorized to amend the guidelines in line with the G.O of this scheme based on the evolving needs of the scheme, feedback from stakeholders, and administrative grounds.

Annexure - I GUIDELINES FOR TAMIL NADU WOMEN ENTREPRENEUR EMPOWERMENT SCHEME (TWEES) 1. Scheme Introduction: The “Tamil Nadu Women Entrepreneur Empowerment Scheme (TWEES)”, is proposed to be launched by the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Department, in line with the announcement (Para No.248) made by the Hon’ble Minister for Finance and Human Resource Development during the presentation of the Budget Estimates 2025 - 2026 to the Legislative Assembly on [unclear figure] March, 2025. The scheme envisions entrepreneurship providing women with the following:- I. Training: Skill development training and entrepreneurial guidance. 11. Entrepreneurial Mentorship: Ongoing guidance and support through Government-nominated business associated mentors. III. Financial Assistance: a. Bank loans up to Rs.10 lakh. b. 25% subsidy (maximum Rs.2 lakh per beneficiary). IV. Handholding Support: Assistance in business registration, compliance, marketing, and scaling up will be done by FaMeTN. 2. Eligibility criteria: I.

Eligibility criteria: I. Women who are domiciled in Tamil Nadu possessing family Ration Card. 11. Age above 18 years not exceeding 55 years. III. No educational qualification is prescribed. IV. Priority to SC/ST, transgender persons, persons with disabilities, widows / destitute widows and women from Below Poverty Line (BPL) families. V. There is no income ceiling applicable for availing benefits under the scheme. ae VI. The scheme will be restricted to one member per family where family refers to father, mother and unmarried children. 3. Activities covered: ji. All economically viable new manufacturing, service and trading activities excluding direct agricultural activities like raising crop, Animal husbandry activities and the negative list of activities prescribed in the MSME Policy [unclear figure] ii. Preference will be given to activities under the Focus/Priority Sectors listed in Annexure-II. The upper investment limit for these sectors may be relaxed on a case-to-case basis. 4. Project cost: (i) The maximum permissible project cost is Rs.10 lakh for new enterprises in the manufacturing, service and business sectors. Project costs include both capital expenditure and working capital. Projects that consist solely of working capital may not be considered. (ii) The Projects of value Rs.2lakh and lesser falling under the specified trades of the KKT scheme may be encouraged in KKT scheme only.

Whereas, KKT women beneficiary who intends to avail loan for their expansion can be top up under this scheme and the difference in subsidy after deducting the subsidy availed under KKT Scheme may be released subject to the condition that minimum 75% of the additional loan is for new asset creation. 5. Promoter’s Contribution: The promoter is required to contribute a minimum of 5% of the total project cost from their own resources. 6. Individual based Subsidy: The subsidy amount will be 25% of the total approved or actual cost of the project, not exceeding Rs.2lakh.Front end subsidy will be released directly to the lending bank upon loan disbursal. 7. Training: i. After the loan is sanctioned, a 3-day mandatory Entrepreneur Development Training will be conducted by the Entrepreneurship Development and Innovation Institute (EDII)-TN. ii. For manufacturing enterprises, based on the demand, skill training shall be provided by the Tamil Nadu Skill Development Corporation (TNSDC). 8. Selection of beneficiaries: Beneficiaries will be screened by the District Task Force Committee, headed by the General Manager of the respective District Industries Centre. 9. The Committee will also decide on projects falling under the Focus/Priority Sectors. 10. Sanction of loan: Sanctioning of projects by the financing bank branches will be subject to an assessment of their financial viability, in line with the recommendations of the Task Force Committee. 11. Financial Institutions: All Commercial banks including Nationalized Banks, Private Sector Banks, Small Finance Banks, NBFCs, TAICO Bank, and other Co-operative Banks. 12. Collateral: No collateral is required. 13. Bank Loan: Banks shall sanction and disburse 95% of the project cost as a loan, which includes the 25% Government subsidy. Banks may also sanction and disburse loans exceeding the recommended project cost; however, the subsidy will be calculated based on the recommended project cost only. 14. Rate of interest: In accordance with banking norms. 15. Repayment period: Repayment period may be for a minimum period of 5 years or as decided by the financing branch after an initial moratorium period of 3 to 6 months. 16. Identification cards or registration certificates issued by other departments will also be leveraged for the same. To simplify the application process, a project report template will be made available on the online portal for applicants to download, complete, and submit. -5- c) There shall be no fees or charges for enrolment under the scheme. d) The applications received online by District Industries Centres will be scrutinizedand shall be placed before the Task Force Committee for selection and recommendation to the banks. e) The Selection will be based on the viability ofthe project. f) The selected applications will be sent to the bank branches for sanction of loan. g) The sanctions given by the banks shall be intimated to the beneficiary under intimation to the concerned District Industries Centres. h) The District Industries Centres shall arrange a mandatory three-day Entrepreneurship Development training program, conducted online and skill training for new entrepreneurs may be provided on demand basis by the Tamil Nadu Skill Development Corporation, Chennai (TNSDC, Chennai). Monitoring framework: a) Physical Verification: With respect to follow up and to know the impact of the scheme and to ensure proper utilization of Government subsidy, on expiry of one year of implementation of the scheme, a performance audit of 5% of beneficiaries shall be conducted through an independent agency. b) Review and Monitoring: The progress of the Scheme will be reviewed by the District Collector at the Bankers Standing Committee, District Level Co-ordination Committee (DLCC) /District Level Review Committee (DLRC) meetings conducted periodically with the Bankers. items.text: ABSTRACT Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises – Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme – Introduction of New Scheme – Orders – Issued. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (D2) Department G.O.(Ms).No. 80 Dated: 30.07.2010 Read: The Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce, Rc.No. 3111/DIC3/2010, dated 16.04.2010. --------- ORDER: Micro, Small and Medium Industries Policy 2008, has a vision to promote ten lakh direct and indirect employment opportunities during Eleventh Plan period. The objective is to create employment opportunities particularly to the vulnerable sections of the society and rural people with a view to ensuring inclusive development. 2. In his letter read above the Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce has sent a proposal for introduction of a new scheme, namely “Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme”.

items.text: 2. In his letter read above the Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce has sent a proposal for introduction of a new scheme, namely “Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme”. The scheme aims to mitigate the unemployment problems of socially and economically weaker sections of the society, particularly among the educated and unemployed to become self employed by setting up Manufacturing / Service / Business enterprises by availing loan upto the maximum of Rs.5 lakhs, Rs. 3 lakhs and Rs. 1 lakh respectively, with subsidy assistance from the State Government upto 15% of the project cost. This scheme was also announced on the floor the Assembly during Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Demand for 2010-11. 3. The Government, after careful consideration, approve the scheme of “Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme” as appended to this order for implementation from the year 2010-11 onwards. The Government also agree to provide a sum of Rs.17.00 crores for the year 2010-11 towards state’s assistance for the above scheme. 2 4. This order issue with the concurrence of Finance department vide its U.O.No. 38360/Ind/2010, dated 29.07.2010. (BY ORDER OF THE GOVERNOR) P. SELVAM, ADDITIONAL CHIEF SECRETARY TO GOVERNMENT. Stock file / Spare copy. //FORWARDED BY ORDER// SECTION OFFICER 3 ANNEXURE UNEMPLOYED YOUTH EMPLOYMENT GENERATION PROGRAMME 1. Preamble Hon’ble Chief Minister released an exclusive Policy for the development of Micro, Small and Medium Industries in the State viz. “Micro, Small and Medium Industries Policy 2008” on 22.02.2008, with the objective of targeting a sustained annual growth rate of over 10% for Micro, Small and Medium Industries and thereby creating 10 lakh direct and indirect employment opportunities during the XI Plan period. In order to achieve the above objective, Government have announced a bouquet of incentive schemes in the Micro, Small and Medium Industries Policy for creation of infrastructure facilities and to provide subsidy assistance, marketing and technical support for the growth of Micro, Small and Medium Industries in the State. The Government, with a view to create employment opportunities to the socially and economically backward strata of the society as envisaged in the Micro, Small and Medium Industries Policy, has formulated the Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme (UYEGP). The scheme is intended to mitigate the unemployment problems of socially and economically weaker sections of the society, particularly among the educated and unemployed to become self employed by setting up Manufacturing / Service / Business enterprises by availing loan upto the maximum of Rs. 5 lakhs, Rs. 3 lakhs and Rs.

items.text: 5 lakhs, Rs. 3 lakhs and Rs. 1 lakh respectively, with subsidy assistance from the State Government upto 15% of the project cost. 2. Objectives : 1. To generate employment opportunities for the educated unemployed in their native places itself, by setting of self employment ventures in Micro enterprises in Manufacturing Service and Business sectors. 2. Preventing mass migration from rural areas to urban areas due to unemployment. 3. To provide livelihood opportunities to the marginalized people in rural and urban areas. 4. To facilitate provision of collateral free advances under Credit Guarantee Trust for Micro, Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) dovetailing under Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme. 3. The Parameters of the Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme scheme: 4 i) Nodal Agency : The Commissionerate of Industries and Commerce is the Nodal Agency at State level to implement the scheme across the state. ii) Areas of Operation: The scheme is applicable to all areas in the State including rural and urban areas. iii) Implementing agencies: District Industries Centre (DICs) of the concerned Districts and the Office of the Regional Joint Director of Industries and Commerce in respect of Chennai District will be the implementing agencies for the Scheme. 4. Eligibility Criteria i) Any individual, above 18 years of age. ii) The family income of the beneficiary along with the spouse shall not exceed Rs.1,50,000/- per annum, as declared by the applicant duly certified by the Notary Public / Oath Commissioner. 5. Preference : Preference will be given to weaker sections including women, minorities, transgender, physically challenged persons.

items.text: 5. Preference : Preference will be given to weaker sections including women, minorities, transgender, physically challenged persons. The number of Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribes beneficiaries should not be less than 19% (18+1), 30% for Backward Classes (BCs) and 20% for Most Backward Classes and Denotified Communities (MBC & DCs). In case, Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribes / Backward Classes / Most Backward Classes and Denotified Communities candidates are not available, District Industries Centres will be competent to consider other categories of candidates under Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme. The preference given under various categories will not be carried over to the next financial year. 6. Maximum Project cost: Rs. 5.00 lakhs for manufacturing sector, Rs.3.00 lakhs for service sector and Rs.1.00 lakh for business sector. 7. Promoter’s Contribution: 10% for General Category as owner’s contribution. 5 5% for special category (viz. Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribes / Backward Classes / Most Backward Classes / Minorities / Women / Ex-servicemen / Physically Challenged / Transgender) as owners’ contribution. 8. Subsidy: Subsidy at rate of 15% of the project cost will be sanctioned to the beneficiaries. 9. Activities covered: All economically viable manufacturing, service and business activities excluding direct agricultural operations like raising crop etc., 10.Training: 7 days training in Entrepreneur Development Programme to be conducted by Entrepreneur Development Institute (EDI) of Government of Tamil Nadu is mandatory. However, the training shall be completed within 12 months from the date of selection by the District Task Force Committees (DTFCs).

However, the training shall be completed within 12 months from the date of selection by the District Task Force Committees (DTFCs). 11.Target / per year Manufacturing - 5,000 beneficiaries Service - 3,000 beneficiaries Business - 2,000 beneficiaries TOTAL - 10,000 beneficiaires 12.How to apply: The scheme will be advertised through print and electronic media. The beneficiary can submit application along with project profile, at the respective District Industries Centre with copies of certificates in proof of educational qualification, nativity, community, Ex-servicemen (wherever applicable) and proof for physically challenged. The beneficiaries can also file their applications through online. 13.Selection of Beneficiaries: Beneficiaries will be selected through interview process by the District Task Force Committee headed by the General Manager of the concerned District Industries Centre. 14.Task force Committee 6 Chairman : General Manager, District Industries Centre Members : Lead bank District Manager, Tamil Nadu Adi Dravidar Housing and Development Corporation Limited (TAHDCO) District Coordinators from Leading Banks in the Districts Representative from District Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Associations Representative from National Small Industries Corporation Limited / Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises-Development Institute District Employment Officer Representative of Project Officer, District Rural Development Agency Representative of Project Officer, Magalir Thittam. 15.Project sanction: Project will be sanctioned by financing branches of the Banks as per techno-economic viability. 16.Financial Institutions:

items.text: 15.Project sanction: Project will be sanctioned by financing branches of the Banks as per techno-economic viability. 16.Financial Institutions: All Nationalised Banks, Private Sector Banks and Tamil Nadu Industrial Co-operative Bank. 17.Collateral: No collateral is required. 18.Amount of the Bank Loan: Banks sanction and release 90-95% loan of the project cost. (Including Government subsidy of 15%) 19.Rate of interest: Normal Bank rate of interest. 20.Repayment period: Repayment Schedule shall be for 5 years after an initial moratorium period of 6 months or date of commencement of project whichever is earlier. 21.Defaulter 7 Should not be a defaulter to any nationalized bank / financial institution / Co-operative bank. Further, a person already assisted under other subsidy linked Government schemes would not be eligible under this scheme. 22.Operation of the Scheme  Project proposals in the prescribed application format with relevant details will be invited from the unemployed / potential beneficiaries at District level through pre-selection motivation campaigns, walk in Interviews by the District Industries Centres.  The applications received by District Industries Centres will be scrutinized and shall be placed before the Task Force Committee at least once in a month.  The Selection will be based on the experience, qualification, skill, viability of the project, marketability etc.,  The selected applications will be sent to the bank branches to the total numbers not less than 125% of the target fixed by the Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce from time to time.  The bank branches shall call for personal interview with the applications to provide subsequent provisional sanction by them.

items.text: The provisional sanctions shall be intimated to the concerned District Industries Centres.  The District Industries Centres shall arrange for compulsory Entrepreneur Development Programme training for a period of seven days by the Entrepreneur Development Institute and on completion, Entrepreneur Development Institute will issue training certificates.  After successful completion of Entrepreneur Development Programme training, the beneficiary will deposit the Promoter’s Contribution with the bank. Thereafter, the bank will disburse the 1 st installment of the bank finance to the beneficiary on production of the training completion certificates.  The respective disbursement advices should be forwarded to District Industries Centres along with the subsidy claims.  The Tamil Nadu Government subsidy amount should be drawn by the Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce and disbursed to all the Districts where it will be deposited with the lead district Bank and they will act as District Level Nodal Bank. Interest accrual, if any, shall be adjusted against sanction of the contingency fund.  On receipt of Subsidy claim raised by the financing branch duly countersigned by the General Manager, District Industries Centre, District Nodal Bank will release the subsidy to financing bank branches.  The subsidy will be deposited in a Term Deposit Receipt (TDR) for 3 years at the financing bank branch level in the name of the beneficiary. No interest will be paid on the Term Deposit Receipt and no interest will be charged on loan amount equal to the amount of Term Deposit Receipt.

At the State level, the progress of the Scheme will be monitored by the State Level Bankers Committee (SLBC).

items.text: At the State level, the progress of the Scheme will be monitored by the State Level Bankers Committee (SLBC). The Additional Chief Secretary to Government, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Department will also review the State level performance of the Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme Scheme on quarterly basis as the Chairman of the Committee. 26.Backward & Forward Linkages: As a support service, funds will be provided by Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce in Government of Tamil Nadu for Backward & Forward Linkages under the scheme. 27.Publicity: Seminars to be conducted in each district for creating awareness of Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme in the area in the form of pre-selection motivation campaigns / Walk-in-interviews. 9 28.Funds: Training / Contingency Expenses per beneficiary will be sanctioned as indicated below:- 1. Stipend for Trainees Rs. 500.00 2. Fee for Training Institutions Rs. 750.00 3. Contingency Fund Rs. 250.00 Besides this, fund will be sanctioned for publicity expenses towards State Level Workshop, District Level Workshop, District Level awareness compassion and Printing and Publicity charges for the scheme. The contingency fund will be utilized for the following activities:- 1. Printing of forms. 2. Stationery. 3. Correspondence. 4. Petrol, Oil and Lubricants. 5. Hiring of transport. 6. Preparation of project profiles. 7. Organising workshops. 8. Course fee for attending Regional Level workshops. 9. Ten percentage of the contingency fund will be apportioned to Central Office. P. items.text: Order: In the G.O. first read above, the Government approved the Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme and issued orders to implement the scheme from the year 2010-11 onwards with maximum ceiling project cost of Rs.5 lakh for manufacturing sector, Rs. 3 lakh for service sector and Rs.1 lakh for business sector. 2. In the G.O. second read above, the Government have enhanced the rate of Subsidy from 15% to 25% of the project cost from the year 2014-15 with effect from 01.04.2014 and the maximum subsidy amount has been enhanced from Rs.75000/- to Rs.1,25,000/- per beneficiary under Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme (UYEGP). 2 3. In the G.O. third read above, the Government have enhanced the Maximum eligible project cost from Rs.5.00 lakh to Rs.10.00 lakh under Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme (UYEGP) for the Manufacturing Sector with restriction on the Maximum subsidy amount to Rs 1.25 lakh. 4. In his proposal fourth read above, the Principal Secretary / Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce has stated that the representations are received from the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises associations and General Managers, District Industries Centres and many projects above Rs.1 lakh under Business Category and above Rs.3 lakh under Service Category could not be considered, due to the reason that the guidelines did not permit.

items.text: The above issue has been discussed with the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Associations and General Managers, District Industries Centres and the following amendments are suggested. i) Enhancing the Maximum project cost under business and service category to Rs.5.00 lakh from the existing limit of Rs.1.00 Lakh and Rs.3.00 lakh respectively. ii) Extending the subsidy @ 25% of the project cost without any restrictions on the upper ceiling. iii) | Enhancing the eligibility criteria of family annual income limit from Rs.1.50 lakh to Rs.5.00 lakh. Further the justification for enhancing the project cost is as follows: - i) The scheme was approved by Government in 2010-11. Due to cost escalation, the projects cannot be setup with the same amount at the present rates. ii) To cover more beneficiaries under Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP). iii) To increase the employment generation if the average project cost is increased. — iv) To increase the employment generation in rural and urban areas since Business and Service activities normally flourished in these areas and thereby restricting the migration of people from rural to urban areas. 5. The Government after careful examination of the above proposal of the Principal Secretary / Industries Commissioner and Director of Industries and Commerce has decided to accept it and accordingly issue the following orders: - i) The maximum project cost is enhanced under Business category to Rs.5 lakh from Rs.1 lakh and under Services category to Rs.5 lakh from Rs.3 lakh. ii) The eligibility criteria of family annual income limit is enhanced to Rs.5 lakh from Rs.1.50 lakh. 3 6.
